0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Children of the Abandoned are a secretive and enigmatic group bound by a strict code of conduct and a deeply rooted philosophy of anonymity and solidarity. Their name stems from a foundational belief: that they, like many of society’s forgotten, have been forsaken by the world but have found unity and purpose within their fellowship.
The group began centuries ago, in the year 555, in Laugstrond (City), the capital city of The Principality of Laugstrond within the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation). Amid the widespread war and social upheaval of the time, a knight named Eryndor the Forlorn, returning from battle, discovered a group of abandoned children struggling to survive in the ruins of a once-prosperous city. Struck by their plight and disillusioned by the horrors of war, Eryndor vowed to protect these children and offer them a new way of life. Over time, these children grew into a tightly knit community, adopting Eryndor’s values of discipline, unity, and self-reliance. From this humble beginning, the Children of the Abandoned emerged as a structured and enduring fellowship.
A defining characteristic of the Children is their helmets. Each member wears a sealed helmet that completely hides their face from view, an unbroken symbol of their shared identity and their renunciation of individual distinction in service to the collective. The helmet is kept on at all times and is only removed for food, sleep, or in complete solitude. Should a member’s face be seen by another, it is considered a deep dishonour, one that severs their connection to the group permanently.
The practice of wearing helmets symbolizes the rejection of ego and personal vanity, creating equality among members regardless of origin or status. To the Children of the Abandoned, no face carries greater significance than another, and every action taken while wearing the helmet reflects on the group as a whole.
One of the group’s unique practices is the adoption of orphans and children living on the streets into their fold. This serves not only to sustain their numbers but also to offer a sense of belonging to those who have been cast aside by society. These children are raised with the group’s teachings and traditions, learning the value of anonymity, solidarity, and discipline. They are given a helmet of their own when they come of age, marking their full initiation into the fellowship.
Outsiders often view the Children of the Abandoned with suspicion or fear, largely due to their secrecy and unconventional ways. Rumours abound of strange rituals and hidden motives, though few have ever truly understood their philosophy. To the Children, such misconceptions are irrelevant; their loyalty lies within their own ranks and to the mission they serve, whatever form it may take.
Despite their mystique, the Children of the Abandoned are known for their resilience and the disciplined cohesion of their members. While their true numbers and full intentions remain uncertain, their acts, whether mercenary work, charity, or vengeance, speak to a group unified by unshakable conviction.

Eryndor the Forlorn

Tazdu Varross

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Church of Absolution is a minor religious organisation that spread throughout Fera beginning in the late 1600's to the Modern era.
Their belief is that all creatures, beings and things were created by a unifying power. This unifying power they call "The God" but is actually what that most call the Aether. In their modern era they are not aggressive against other religions as they see it as an extension of the "One True God".
The Church began as a mix of various Monster Hunters, Entitled (Class) Hunters and would keep 'regular' people safe and even into the Modern time setting, the Church has various secret organisations within its ranks defending the world from Monsters and the damaging effects of the Aether. One such organisation is "The Sinners". An all female unit of assassins and warriors.

Gregory Novak

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Order of the Weighted Souls is an ancient brotherhood of warrior monks who serve as peacekeepers, arbiters, and last-resort enforcers of law throughout the realm. Unlike knights or mercenaries, they do not seek battle, but when forced to kill, they bear the ultimate burden: the name of the slain is etched into their very identity.

Lothar Völsung
Hagen Falkenrath
Siegfried Drachenholt
Wulfram Eisenhart
Alaric von Himmelsbruch
Reinhardt Sturmfels
Eckhart Grimmwald
Valter von Dornhelm
Gerwulf Schattenberg
Dietmar Blutstern
The Order believes that every life taken leaves a spiritual weight upon the soul. Killing, even in the name of justice, is an act of sorrow rather than triumph. To ensure that no death is forgotten, a member of the Order takes on the name of the person they have slain, binding their memory to themselves for eternity. Over time, these monks accumulate names like shackles, each one a reminder of the life they could not spare. The more names a monk carries, the heavier their spirit becomes.

The Unburdened – Initiates who have yet to take a life. They train in philosophy, diplomacy, and combat, preparing for the day when they must bear their first name.
The Nametaken – Warriors who have killed and carry at least one name. Their armour and robes are marked with symbols representing those they have slain.
The Veilbearers – Senior monks who carry so many names that they wear veils over their faces, symbolizing their growing detachment from their own identity.
The Weighed – Masters of the Order, those who carry the greatest burden. Some are said to have more names than they can remember, their original identity long lost. They serve as wandering sages, offering guidance and judgment in the most dire matters.

To Take a Life is to Take a Name. No member of the Order may kill without consequence. Every name taken must be recorded in the Order’s sacred ledger.
Violence is the Last Resort. Diplomacy, wisdom, and restraint are the preferred tools of the Weighted Souls. A monk who kills too freely risks expulsion, or worse.
The Burden is Personal. A warrior monk may never surrender or discard a name once taken. It is theirs to carry until death.
No King Commands the Weighed. The Order serves peace, not politics. They may advise rulers but swear no allegiance to any crown.
Members of the Order wear dark, unadorned robes, often embroidered with the names they carry. Their weapons are designed for subduing rather than killing—staves, weighted chains, and blunt-edged swords. Only in the gravest necessity do they draw a killing blade, often engraved with a prayer for the soul it will claim.
If a monk ever forgets a name, either through age or arrogance, it is said that their soul becomes untethered, cursed to wander in the afterlife until they can reclaim what was lost. Some among the Weighed are known to retreat into solitude, whispering names in the dark to keep them alive.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld

The Rings of The Örtüer are various bands of various metals with various gems and stones inlaid into the metal.
One may look like a simple golden band with no adornment while another might hold the clearest of diamonds in its clasp.
The figure whom wears the ring will take no appearance changes, at first.
After some time, the figure's skin would become pallid and grey, turning white until it faded entirely. The mind and soul of the creature gone and bound to the ring. They would appear in void black robes, chain mail and plate armour under the vast layers of smoke like robes.
The Örtüer are unyielding, untiring. Their former souls and minds all but gone in the latter stages of the transformation.
The Örtüer are the weapons of their master, once mortal figures given rings of power by the vile Kräl Şah Yilmazok Akar . These ten rings gave great power to their wielder but twisted their minds and bodies; drove them to give themselves to their master.
In the later years, after Kräl Şah Yilmazok Akar 's reign of terror was defeated by 3. The Nine Divines , some of the rings went into the hands of the Human's whom fought to defeat him. Warlords and powerful mortals took possession of the Rings and were soon driven again to destruction.
Throughout the years the rings passed from legend to legend, soon captured and hidden by a band of adventurers .

Nizar
Anthonius
Ia
Asardin
Salasid
Namtar
Aslaner
Karya
Ukran
Lisakr

Vlandirleld Amberster
Elegosa
Xandril

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
A gang of teenage students who enter dreams to plan heists and steal information.
When 16-year-old Maximilian Schmidt discovers that he can enter people's dreams, he sees it as an opportunity to pull off the perfect heist. With the help of his friends – a group of mischievous teens known as the "Lucid Heisters" – Max delves into the subconscious of wealthy individuals to plan elaborate thefts. But as the group becomes more successful, they draw the attention of the law and a rival group of dream thieves. As the stakes become higher, Max must decide how far he's willing to go for his criminal pursuits and if it's worth sacrificing his own morals and relationships.

Clara Voigt - "The Voice"
Julian Köhler - "The Brawn"
Frieda Köhler - "The Heart"
Finn Röder - Lockpicker - "The Touch"
Niesenn Von Durchhusen - The Hand

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Formal Title:
Department Z – Residual, Discredited, and Terminal Casework
Common Usage:
“Z-Dept”
“Sent to Z”
“Filed under Z”
Meaning in Practice:
Where cases go when they are:
Politically inconvenient
Scientifically impossible
Too dangerous to close properly
The administrative equivalent of a graveyard
In Imperium slang:
“If it’s in Z, it’s dead.”
Which is, of course, a lie.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Parliament of Princes is one of two ruling Parliaments of the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation) with the other being The Parliament of the People.
Filled with the various Princes of the Principalities of the Imperium, it is the last process of a vote on a Law before it is sent to the Imperator for final vote and ratification into Law.
The Head of The Parliament of Princes, voted on by its members and the one who presides over the ceremony and the handing of the Law to the Imperator is known as The Prince Elect
It was formed as a concequence of The First Principality War and became a unifying idea to the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation) as a whole
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.author: Lewis Stockton

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Big Buster Burgers is an Ilmarian fast-food chain specializing in flame-grilled, oversized burgers, crispy fries, and thick milkshakes. Known for its bold flavours and generous portions, offering a signature Buster Sauce and an extra-large Buster Burger that’s stacked high with toppings.
Slogan: "Bigger Bites, Bigger Flavor!"
🍔 Big Buster Burger – A double-patty burger with melted cheese, crispy bacon, and signature Buster Sauce.
🍟 Mega Crunch Fries – Extra crispy, seasoned fries served with dipping sauces.
🥤 Buster Blitz Shake – Thick, creamy shakes in classic and wild seasonal flavours.
🐔 Crispy Buster Chicken – Juicy, hand-breaded chicken sandwiches and tenders.
🌯 Buster Wraps – Grilled or crispy chicken wraps with fresh veggies and sauces.
🔥 Limited-time "Monster Buster" burgers with crazy, over-the-top toppings.
📱 App-based rewards program with discounts and free meal rewards.
🍔 Drive-thru and mobile ordering for quick service.

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Bite & Bolt is a Pawhye (Continent) high-energy fast food chain focused on bold flavours and lightning-fast service. It combines the speed of traditional fast food with fresh, high-quality ingredients and a menu built for people on the go. With a sleek, modern design and a commitment to fire-grilled burgers, crispy chicken, and zesty sauces, Bite & Bolt is the perfect stop for those who want something quick without sacrificing taste.
Slogan: "Fast. Fresh. Fired Up!"
🔥 Bolt Burger – A flame-grilled, juicy beef patty with melted cheese, crispy onions, and signature Bolt Sauce on a toasted brioche bun.
🍗 Thunder Strips – Extra crispy, hand-breaded chicken tenders served with a choice of house-made dipping sauces.
🌯 Lightning Wrap – Spicy grilled chicken, fresh veggies, and tangy Zing Sauce wrapped in a warm tortilla.
🍟 Crispy Bolt Fries – Golden, seasoned fries with a side of Fiery Ranch or Bite Sauce for dipping.
🥤 Blitz Shakes – Thick, creamy milkshakes in Power Chocolate, Shock Strawberry, and Vanilla Voltage flavours.
⚡ "Bolt Mode" Meals – Customers can add extra spice, cheese, or double meat for a bigger, bolder experience.
📱 Fast-Track Ordering – Mobile app orders are ready in minutes, and drive-thru service is ultra-efficient.
🎉 Limited-Time Shock Specials – Seasonal menu items featuring wild, over-the-top flavours.

A modern, urban aesthetic with sleek black and red branding, neon signage, and high-energy music in stores.
Mascot: Blitz the Cheetah – a lightning-fast, stylish cheetah who embodies speed and flavour.

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Gravy Train Diner is an Umissian Southern-style fast food joint serving up hearty comfort food at lightning speed. Specializing in crispy fried chicken, fluffy biscuits, homestyle mashed potatoes, and—of course—rich, flavorful gravy, this spot is all about big portions, bold flavors, and down-home hospitality. Whether you're craving a classic biscuits & gravy breakfast or a gravy-smothered burger, the Gravy Train is always rolling!
Slogan: "Smothered, Southern, and Satisfying!"
🍗 The Conductor’s Combo – A crispy, golden-fried chicken sandwich topped with buttermilk gravy, pickles, and spicy honey on a toasted brioche bun.
🍔 Gravy Slinger Burger – A juicy, flame-grilled burger topped with cheddar, bacon, and smothered in country gravy.
🥔 Loaded Train Tots – Crispy tater tots drenched in cheese, gravy, and bacon bits, with a side of ranch.
🥞 Biscuits & Gravy Bomb – Buttery, homemade biscuits piled high with sausage gravy and served with a side of crispy hash browns.
🌯 Southern Wrap Express – A soft tortilla packed with fried chicken, mac & cheese, and gravy for a handheld comfort meal.
🥤 Sweet Rail Shakes – Thick, Southern-style milkshakes in flavors like Peach Cobbler, Pecan Pie, and Bourbon Vanilla.
🚂 "Full Steam" Option – Double the gravy or add extra toppings to any meal!
📱 Gravy Train Rewards – Earn free sides, drinks, or meals through an easy-to-use mobile app.
🎉 "Gravy of the Month" Specials – Seasonal gravy flavors like Cajun Gravy, Smoky BBQ Gravy, and Maple Bacon Gravy.

Rustic, diner-style aesthetic with vintage train decor, warm lighting, and a cozy but fast-paced atmosphere.
Mascot: Gravy Gus – A friendly, moustached train conductor who’s always ready to serve up delicious, gravy-smothered goodness.
Drive-Thru Tagline: "All Aboard for Flavour!"

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
NomNom Express is a globally inspired fast food chain that brings bold flavours from around the world to a quick-service setting. With a focus on fresh ingredients, fusion flavours, and lightning-fast service, NomNom Express is the perfect stop for foodies on the go. Whether you’re craving Kokkan street food, Umissian-inspired bites, or classic Ilmarian comfort, there’s something for every craving at NomNom!
Slogan: "Fast. Fresh. Flavor-Packed!"
🌯 Global Crunch Wrap – A crispy tortilla stuffed with spicy chicken, melted cheese, crunchy slaw, and NomNom Sauce, pressed to perfection.
🍜 Noodle NomBox – Stir-fried noodles tossed in savoury soy-garlic sauce, with a choice of grilled chicken, beef, or tofu.
🍔 Kokka Teriyaki Burger – A flame-grilled beef patty with teriyaki glaze, crispy onions, and wasabi mayo on a brioche bun.
🍚 Rice Bowl Rush – A hearty bowl of jasmine rice, sweet & spicy grilled chicken, veggies, and NomNom Yum Sauce.
🥟 Express Dumplings – Steamed or crispy dumplings filled with pork, chicken, or veggie goodness, served with ginger soy dip.
🍟 Street Cart Fries – Golden fries topped with queso, sriracha aioli, cilantro, and pickled onions.
🥤 Bubble Blitz Drinks – A variety of Boba teas, Thai iced tea, and fruit refreshers for a sweet, chewy sip.
🚄 “Speedy Combos” – Customizable meal sets with a main, side, and drink for people on the move.
📱 NomNom Rewards – Collect points for every order and redeem free meals, exclusive items, or secret menu deals.
🔥 Limited-Time “Around the World” Specials – Rotating menu items featuring flavours from different cultures, such as Kokkan BBQ Tacos, Ilmarian Pita Wraps, or Umissian Butter Chicken Bowls.

A modern, high-energy aesthetic with sleek red-and-black branding, neon signage, and an urban street food vibe.
Mascot: Nomi the Panda – A playful, globe-trotting panda who loves discovering new flavours.
Drive-Thru Tagline: "Next Stop: Flavour!"

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Sizzle & Dash is a grill-focused fast food joint that delivers bold, smoky flavours at lightning speed. Specializing in fire-grilled burgers, sizzling steaks, charred chicken, and flame-kissed veggies, it’s the ultimate stop for those who crave that fresh-off-the-grill taste without the wait. Whether you're dining in, dashing through the drive-thru, or grabbing a quick bite on the go, Sizzle & Dash guarantees flame, flavor, and freshness—fast!
Slogan: "Hot Off the Grill, Fast to Your Hands!"
🔥 Blazing Sizzle Burger – A juicy, flame-grilled beef patty topped with pepper jack cheese, crispy bacon, fire-roasted jalapeños, and Sizzle Sauce on a toasted brioche bun.
🐔 Dash Chicken Sandwich – Charred grilled chicken breast, smoky BBQ sauce, Swiss cheese, and slaw on a fresh potato bun.
🥩 Steak Sizzle Wrap – Sliced, fire-seared steak, caramelized onions, grilled peppers, and creamy garlic aioli wrapped in a warm tortilla.
🌮 Flame-Grilled Tacos – Street-style tacos with charred steak or chicken, fresh cilantro, lime, and spicy chipotle crema.
🍟 Sizzle Fries – Crispy, hand-cut fries topped with melted cheese, smoky chipotle ranch, and crumbled bacon.
🥗 Smoky Southwest Salad – Grilled chicken, fire-roasted corn, black beans, avocado, and crunchy tortilla strips, drizzled with tangy lime dressing.
🥤 Dash Blasts – Refreshing frozen drinks in flavors like Mango Fire, Berry Blaze, and Citrus Thunder.
🔥 "Turn Up the Heat" Option – Add an extra spicy kick to any meal with habanero sauce, ghost pepper seasoning, or fire-roasted chilies.
📱 Sizzle & Dash Express App – Order ahead, earn rewards, and access secret menu items.
🌍 Grill Master Specials – Monthly rotating grilled dishes inspired by international flavors, such as Korean BBQ Bowls, Mediterranean Lamb Wraps, or Jamaican Jerk Chicken Bites.

A bold, modern aesthetic with sleek metallic tones, red flames in the branding, and an open-flame kitchen visible to customers.
Mascot: Blitz the Inferno Fox – A sleek, fiery fox who’s always on the move, bringing the heat wherever he goes.
Drive-Thru Tagline: "Sizzling in Seconds!"

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Snack Shinsō is a Kokkan-inspired fast food joint that blends traditional flavours with modern, high-speed service. With a menu full of crispy tempura, flame-seared meats, savoury rice bowls, and handcrafted sushi-inspired bites, Snack Shinsō delivers quick, flavourful meals that honour the spirit of the samurai. Whether you're grabbing a quick bento box, slurping up some noodles, or indulging in umami-packed street food, Snack Shinsō ensures that every bite is worthy of a warrior!
Slogan: "Master the Art of Flavour!"
🍙 Shinsō Rice Bombs – Crispy-fried rice balls stuffed with teriyaki chicken, spicy tuna, or miso pork, served with dipping sauces.
🍜 Rosutko Ramen Wrap – A savoury noodle wrap filled with slow-braised pork, scallions, and creamy sesame sauce, wrapped in a warm bao-style tortilla.
🥢 Katsu Master Burger – A panko-crusted chicken or pork katsu patty, topped with tangy tonkatsu sauce, cabbage slaw, and wasabi mayo on a toasted bun.
🍛 Shogun Curry Bowl – Rich Kokkan curry served over fluffy rice, with crispy chicken, beef, or tofu.
🥟 Shinsō Street Dumplings – Golden-crisp or steamed gyoza filled with pork, chicken, or shrimp, drizzled with soy-ginger glaze.
🍣 Speedy Sushi Bites – Mini sushi-inspired rolls filled with spicy tuna, avocado, or crispy tempura shrimp, made fresh and fast.
🥤 Shinsō Energy Elixirs – Refreshing matcha teas, yuzu lemonades, and sakura-flavored sodas.
⚔️ "Warrior’s Feast" Combos – Mix and match bowls, snacks, and drinks for a customizable Shinsō meal set.
📱 Shinsō Honour Code Rewards – Earn katanas (points) for every order and unlock free meals, exclusive items, and secret menu rewards.
🔥 "Master’s Challenge" Monthly Special – Limited-time specialty dishes inspired by different regions of Kokka, such as Yuttoashito (City) Miso Ramen, Kokka Street Skewers, or Wuu (City) Yaki-Onigiri.

A sleek, modern aesthetic with red-and-black samurai-inspired branding, neon kanji signage, and a traditional-meets-futuristic vibe.
Mascot: Tenshu the Fox Shinsō – A mystical, armoured animal warrior who represents speed, skill, and flavour mastery.
Drive-Thru Tagline: "Swift. Savoury. Shinsō-Approved!"

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
CENDEX Systems embodies the dark underbelly of military-industrial innovation; an imposing, bureaucratic monolith that blends cutting-edge technology with ruthless corporate pragmatism. It’s the kind of company where breakthroughs come at the price of ethics, and where power is centralized under a cold, calculating leadership, making it as menacing in its procedures as in its products.
CENDEX Systems is a sprawling, shadowy corporate powerhouse specializing in cutting-edge military hardware and advanced artificial intelligence research. Established under the guise of national security, it operates at the intersection of government contracts and private sector innovation, wielding immense influence within defense and intelligence circles.

Acronym Meaning: Centralized Defense eXperiments; emphasizing a tightly controlled, top-down approach to weaponizing experimental technologies for defense applications.
Corporate Culture:
Highly bureaucratic and labyrinthine, CENDEX is notorious for its rigid chain of command, endless internal red tape, and compartmentalized projects where few employees see the bigger picture. Despite its official “research and development” veneer, the company projects an intimidating presence through constant security protocols, surveillance, and aggressive intellectual property enforcement.
Technology Focus:
Military Hardware: Advanced weapon systems, autonomous drones, exoskeleton suits, and next-gen battlefield electronics.
Artificial Intelligence: Autonomous combat AI, predictive battlefield analytics, adaptive cyberwarfare software, and human-machine interface technologies.
Experimental Projects: Often pushing ethical boundaries, including neural augmentation, AI-controlled lethal systems, and biomechanical soldier enhancements.
Public Image:
CENDEX cultivates a carefully polished front as a patriotic contractor working for national defence. Yet behind closed doors, it is feared and resented by whistle-blowers, rival companies, and even government agencies for its ruthlessness, secrecy, and willingness to sacrifice ethics for profit and power.
Menacing Aura:
The company’s headquarters is a fortress-like complex surrounded by high security zones, patrolled by private military contractors and equipped with biometric access controls. Employees are subject to strict non-disclosure agreements, and internal surveillance monitors everything from conversations to biometric data. CENDEX is rumoured to suppress or “disappear” those who cross it or leak sensitive information.
Bureaucratic Web:
Project approval is governed by multiple opaque committees, each with overlapping authority and conflicting interests, designed to stall or accelerate developments as suits the company’s political or financial goals. This bureaucracy breeds an environment where ambitious innovations can become weaponized too quickly or buried to maintain control.

Vigilant Hawk Drone
Autonomous aerial reconnaissance drone with real-time battlefield AI analytics and lethal payload options.
Sentinel EX-9 Combat Exoskeleton
Powered armor suit enhancing soldier strength, speed, and endurance, integrated with adaptive neural control.
Phantom Net AI
Advanced cyberwarfare AI capable of infiltrating enemy networks and launching coordinated digital attacks autonomously.
Cerberus Tactical AI System
Command-and-control AI that assists battlefield commanders by predicting enemy movements and optimizing troop deployments.
Obsidian Cloak Adaptive Camouflage
Nano-fiber suit providing active camouflage that adapts dynamically to surroundings, rendering soldiers nearly invisible.
Reaper MK-IV Autonomous Gunship
AI-piloted aerial attack vehicle equipped with precision targeting and multi-vector attack capabilities.
NeuroLink Combat Interface
Neural implant enabling soldiers to control weapons, drones, and tactical systems with thought commands.
Titan Pulse Directed Energy Weapon
Portable energy weapon firing high-intensity pulses capable of disabling electronics or incapacitating targets.
Cerberus Bio-Monitor
Implantable health and stress sensor for soldiers, feeding real-time physiological data to command AI.
Sentinel Grid Security Network
Integrated AI-driven perimeter defense system combining automated turrets, sensors, and drone patrols for military bases.
Kräl-Husk - AEX-7 “Pioneer Harness”
A Machine Exo-suite developed by CENDEX Systems from Automata technology stolen from The Dread Valley (Region).

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Maritime Mercantile Legion is a highly organized and disciplined mercenary company that operates across the vast oceans of Fera (Planet). Known for its militaristic hierarchy and business-savvy dealings, the Legion combines precision warfare with efficient trade and exploration, making it a formidable force on the high seas.
The Legion is led by a commanding officer known as the "Commodore," with Karlotta Schönbein serving as the second-in-command. Underneath this leadership structure is a strict chain of command, including captains, lieutenants, and specialized officers who oversee various divisions such as naval warfare, logistics, engineering, and exploration. Every member of the crew is rigorously trained in combat and maritime operations.
The flagship of the Legion is a colossal, multi-purpose vessel known as Stählerne Vorhut. Equipped with reinforced hulls for icebreaking, massive cargo holds, and cutting-edge submarines, the ship is capable of navigating any ocean environment, from frigid arctic waters to tropical archipelagos. Smaller escort ships and submarines complete the Legion's fleet, ensuring they are ready for any mission—be it battle, trade, or deep-sea exploration.
The Maritime Mercantile Legion specializes in high-stakes missions, including:
Naval Combat: Defending allied fleets, engaging in private wars, or repelling pirate attacks.
Expeditions: Exploring uncharted waters, searching for valuable resources, and salvaging ancient relics from lost civilizations.
Trade Protection: Escorting valuable cargo shipments for paying clients, ensuring safe passage through dangerous regions.
Mercantile Enterprises: Acting as intermediaries or brokers in trade deals, leveraging their power to negotiate favorable terms for their allies and themselves.
The Legion is feared and respected across Fera. Known for their efficiency, they complete contracts with ruthless precision and unwavering loyalty to their agreements. However, their militaristic nature and expansionist ambitions often put them at odds with other mercenary companies and seafaring nations.
The symbol of the Maritime Mercantile Legion is a crimson trident crossed with a golden anchor, representing their mastery of both war and commerce. Their motto, "Victory in Trade, Supremacy at Sea," reflects their dual focus on military power and financial dominance.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
A Special forces group in the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation). Serving outside of its borders, the 9th in the name is in fact the number of times a unit of this kind was created since the introduction of the Ilmarian Expeditionary Force.
When a task of the upmost importance is needed exceeding an on the ground manpower of more than 500 soldiers, The Special Detachments is formed.
A mixing of the highest quality soldiers from various branches, the Special Detachment acts independent to any branch and is commanded only by the High Marshal of the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation)

Ilyse Spitz

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Equipped with special flight gear, the members of the Special Deep Air Insertion Division were attached to the Imperial High Command of the Ilmarian Imperial Army.
One piece of equipment they are geared with is the "Deep Air Insertion Pack"; a flight suit and pack that was initially powered by a radioactive isotope but later powered by an Aether Crystal.

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld

Ilmarian Imperium (Nation)
"By spark and barrel, I stand.
Where spells falter, I strike.
My will is my aim; my word, my shot.
In silence or thunder, I serve the Imperium’s flame.
No tyrant, no beast, no shadow shall outdraw my resolve.
I am the steel that speaks, the smoke that binds.
I am Gunslinger; mage, marksman, sentinel true.
Until the last shell falls."
"I do not aim with my hand; I aim with my will.
I do not fire with my gun; I fire with my soul.
I do not kill with hatred; I kill with purpose.
I stand, as iron stands; unshaken, unbroken, unbound."

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
During the early years of the 1800's and the latter of the 1700's, the City Watch of most cities were reformed into two separate branches. The Constabulary and the City Watch. The Watch served as the standing army for defence while the Constabulary acted more as a police force.
With new tactics, equipment and procedures, the Constabulary began to use forensics to find criminals and with the use of Firearms, began to be armed with flintlocks pistols in the early days before moving to pistols in the later years.
Dressed in simple civilian clothes or a uniform of Navy Blue / Black trench coats, the officers were quicker, less inconspicuous and agile.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Host-Guard serve as the elite warriors and enforcers of The Kalihenate; hosts chosen not only for strength, but for obedience, presence, and symbolic value. Each one carries an Asalak symbiote, granting them heightened senses, rapid reflexes, and a near-fanatical loyalty. To outsiders, they appear almost divine; to The Kalihenate, they are simply perfected vessels.
Their armour is instantly recognisable.
Their helmets are towering, stylised visors shaped not like literal serpents or birds, but echoing the mythic grandeur of such creatures.
The Kahl-Masks
Sleek, elongated helms with sweeping crests that rise high above the head, resembling ancient god-faces, smooth, expressionless, unnervingly calm. Thin slits glow faintly with the Asalak symbiote’s colour.
The Shyr-Crests
Wide, angular headpieces with flared side-panels and a crown-like ridge, evoking a regal, predatory presence. These are typically worn by commanders or ceremonial guards.
The motifs are abstract, not literal: sweeping lines, flowing curvature, geometric ridges, designed to make the wearer look inhuman, flawless, untouchable.
The armour of the Host-Guard is crafted of lacquered bronze, volcanic glass-ceramic, obsidian plating, or darkened living-metal alloys. Each set is form-fitting, ritualistic, and deeply symbolic.
Layered plates shaped like overlapping scales or feathers, again abstract rather than naturalistic
High gorgets and broad, angular pauldrons that exaggerate the wearer’s silhouette
Ribbed breastplates engraved with Kalihenate glyphs of unity, obedience, and ascension
Heavy greaves and vambraces reinforced to endure immense physical strain
Their armour is designed not just for battle, but for awe. When a phalanx of Host-Guard marches, the overlapping plates produce a deep, resonant chime—almost musical, intentionally unnerving.
While weapons vary by rank and ritual, they commonly wield:
Khal-staves; polearms that discharge bursts of aetheric force
Ritual great spears with obsidian or crystal tips
Hook-blades designed to disable rather than kill, ideal for capturing new hosts
Each weapon is built to exist as both a tool of war and a holy symbol.
Wear towering Shyr-Crests.
Often partially merged with their symbiote for faster communication.
Wear the sleek, elongated Kahl-Masks.
Serve as bodyguards to Asalak overlords and temple guardians.
Less ornate armour, still intimidating smooth helms, fewer engravings.
Used for mass deployments or guarding outer territories.
The Host-Guard operate with eerie synchronicity, often moving or reacting before an order is fully spoken, guided through shared impulses transmitted by their Asalak parasites. Their presence near an Asalak overlord is suffocating; silent, disciplined, unshakably loyal.
They are not merely soldiers.
They are living symbols of The Kalihenate’s power, walking reminders of what happens when a people become vessels for an empire of parasites who consider themselves gods.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Created by Yuri Moltov, Moltov's Principle suggests that the body and mind may be two interconnected facets of the soul, each influencing and shaping the other in a dynamic relationship. According to this philosophy, the intricate connection between the physical and mental aspects of an individual plays a crucial role in defining one's holistic well-being.
In Moltov's perspective, the body serves as the vessel through which the soul interacts with the tangible world. It is the medium for sensory experiences, actions, and expressions. The mind, on the other hand, acts as the bridge between the ethereal essence of the soul and the physical reality it encounters. Thoughts, emotions, and consciousness are considered manifestations of the soul's engagement with the mind.
This principle implies that the state of the body can influence the state of the mind, and vice versa. Physical health, for instance, may impact mental well-being, and a sound mind can contribute to bodily harmony. The intricate interplay between these elements shapes the overall state of the soul, creating a symbiotic relationship where the health and balance of one aspect can have profound effects on the other.
Moltov's followers often delve into practices that seek harmony between the body and mind, recognizing the importance of holistic well-being. Meditation, mindful movement, and other contemplative exercises are embraced as means to foster this balance, aiming to create a unified and integrated experience of the soul.
While Moltov's Principle remains a philosophical concept, its exploration invites individuals to consider the profound interconnectedness of their physical and mental selves, prompting a deeper understanding of the complexities that constitute the human experience.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
A series of rules set down by The Brethren Court (Nation) to keep the Vampire race secret after The Great Vampire Cull resulting in the near extinction of the Vampire nation.

Blood Bonded Unity: The members of The Brethren Court prioritize unity among their kind. They believe in forming strong blood bonds that tie them together as a collective family, fostering loyalty and mutual support.
Eternal Secrecy: The secrecy of vampire existence is paramount. Members of The Brethren Court vow to protect their true nature from outsider knowledge, avoiding unnecessary exposure and maintaining a veil of mystique.
Honour in the Shadows: The Court believes in maintaining a code of honour even in the darkness. They reject unnecessary violence and maintain a sense of integrity, ensuring their actions are justifiable and guided by a strong moral compass.
Knowledge Seekers: Intellectual pursuits are highly encouraged within The Brethren Court. Vampires strive to accumulate knowledge, arts, and culture over their extended lifetimes, contributing to the enrichment of their society.
Legacy of the Night: The Brethren Court takes pride in their lineage and heritage. They pass down stories and wisdom from one generation to the next, fostering a sense of continuity and a connection to their shared history.
Guidance of Elders: Elder vampires hold a position of respect within the Court. Their centuries of experience are considered invaluable, and their guidance is sought for important decisions affecting the community.
Veil Keepers: Members of the Court are tasked with guarding the supernatural balance. They ensure that the existence of other supernatural entities, along with their own, remains hidden from humanity, preventing chaos and panic.
Sanguine Harmony: The Court values a harmonious relationship with the natural world, understanding that the consumption of blood is a sacred act. They commit to feeding responsibly and minimizing their impact on humans and the environment.
Empathy for Mortals: Despite their differences, The Brethren Court values empathy and compassion toward mortals. They recognize the beauty of emotions and experiences and sometimes forge discreet connections to maintain a sense of humanity.
Balance in Feeding: The Court promotes a balanced approach to feeding. They recognize the necessity of blood consumption for survival but encourage members to do so responsibly, avoiding excess that could draw unwanted attention or harm humans.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Silent Chorus is a major faction operating from the central power station within the Tract. They are a highly organized and secretive group, distinguished by their fanatical devotion and unified, almost non-verbal, nature. While they present themselves as guardians of the Tract's core, their true purpose is to maintain control over the aether energy source and expand their influence.
The core belief of the Silent Chorus is that the Aether Dimension is a sacred, living entity, and the Tract is its physical manifestation. They view the original aether experiment as a divine event that revealed a higher truth. Their ultimate goal is to become one with the Aether, achieving a state of collective consciousness. They believe that by protecting the core and controlling the energy output, they are fulfilling the Aether's will and preparing the world for this "ascension." All other factions and individuals are viewed as threats to this singular purpose.
The Silent Chorus uses advanced psychic and technological manipulation to expand its ranks. Instead of traditional recruitment, they rely on a powerful psionic field emanating from the core of the power station. This field uses aether energy to subtly influence the minds of individuals within the Tract, particularly those who are mentally vulnerable.
Their most effective tool is a psychological conditioning that creates the illusion of communication. Fanatics like Nomad hear directives as a "voice" transmitted through devices like broken radios, even without a power source. This method of control makes followers believe they are acting on their own free will, while in reality they are mere puppets of the faction's leadership, led by the enigmatic Colonel.
The Silent Chorus is hostile to all other groups operating within the Tract, particularly Trackers and scientists. They see anyone attempting to harvest artifacts or study the aether as a desecration of a sacred site. Their well-armed military forces are tasked with sabotaging rival operations and eliminating anyone who gets too close to the core. The faction's fanatical devotion and ability to manipulate their environment make them the most dangerous and unpredictable enemy in the Tract.

The Colonel

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
A Wayrider, from the old word "Wegenreiter". The Wayrider is a figure carved from the bark of the old world; stoic, solitary, and tireless. A guardian of the forgotten paths and worn trails that wind through the deep woods, rugged hills, and borderlands between towns. Neither knight nor outlaw, he serves no crown, yet commands the respect of both peasant and noble.
He is the last to tread the road after sunset, and often the first to rise with the frost.
Wayriders are:
Messengers between isolated hamlets and towns where no post reaches.
Road-guards who escort the desperate through forest passes.
Survivors, walking in lands where others fear to camp.
In some regions, they are hired; in others, they simply arrive. No one knows how they choose their paths. Some say they are exiled soldiers, others say cursed men paying off old debts. Some say its for money.
In folk tales, a Wayrider’s arrival means change; sometimes salvation, sometimes doom.
Children say they ride with ghosts.
Old women leave out bread near road markers, hoping the Wayrider will keep the wolves away.

Hans von Fernweg, "Hans 'Of the Far Road.'"

Born an 'Arizali (Insult)', a 'Defect', Alynae was born blind, as per the custom of the Yaralti people, she was supposed to be killed at birth, however her mother and father went into hiding, bringing up the girl in secret away from anyone else.
After her family were murdered by bandits from the surface, the girl was taken as a slave. Soon rescued by a travelling assassin known as Shadow, she began to train in the art of assassination; however this brought the attention of several demonic creatures that sensed a power within Alynae.
Alynea Helviar is a vision of quiet otherworldliness, her Yaralti heritage marked by smooth, light blue skin that seems to shimmer faintly beneath certain lights; like moonlight diffused through deep water. Her long, white hair cascades freely down her back, often loose or lightly braided, a stark contrast against the darker tones of her travelling garb. Her eyes, clouded and sightless, are pale opalescent orbs—empty of vision yet oddly luminous, giving her a ghostly, almost divine countenance. She moves with an eerie grace, each step deliberate and balanced, guided not by sight but by some inner perception that borders on supernatural. Her clothing is practical yet ceremonial in design: layered silks and leathers, muted greys and indigos, adorned with faint sigils from her Yaralti lineage. To those who encounter her, Alynea appears as both exile and oracle—fragile in form, formidable in presence.
Alynea Helviar is defined by quiet resilience and sharpened instinct. Life has taught her to listen—to the air, to movement, to hearts beating in the dark—and through that listening she has learned to see in ways others cannot. She speaks little, preferring the economy of silence, her words calm and deliberate when they come. Beneath her soft-spoken exterior lies a survivor’s strength, born from the pain of loss and captivity. She harbours a deep distrust of others, though not out of bitterness—rather, from the understanding that kindness is often fleeting. Yet, despite all she has endured, Alynea possesses an almost sacred composure: a gentleness that disarms, and a strange serenity that unsettles even demons. Those close to her sense the vastness of something ancient stirring beneath her calm—a power she neither sought nor fully understands, but which seems inexorably drawn to her.

Karanlik Taraf - Home City
Adestein (City)
It was early into the 1200's of the Imperial age and Alynae Helviar was hiding in the outskirts of the vast Kräl Şah Yilmazok Akar. They have lived in peace and tranquillity, hidden from all other creatures in Fera (Planet)'s Underground.
The young girl was a mistake, an Arizali (Insult). A defect.
Born blind, she should have been strangled at birth with her very own cord, that was what should have happened. Her parents had been out of town when the birth happened and had given birth in one of the many off shoot caves surround the city; out here there had been no Gene-Inspectors to end her life.
That day had been 16 years ago and now the girl was a thriving teenager; although hidden from the rest of her people, she enjoyed her life with her family. Sure the caves were dangerous and her parents kept a short leash on her; she had slowly been learning her Aetherial arts thanks to her mothers teachings.
The day that her life was turned upside down had come and gone so fast she did not know what happened. All she knew was that she had lost her mother and father; were they dead or were they alive? She did not know.
All that she knew was that she had been taken by these.... 'umans' what ever her father had called them.
It had been days and she was exhausted, cold and afraid; the fear of the unknown had set in imedietly but it had sort of faded a little now.
It did not stop the girl from being scared; these foul smelling and foul-speaking things did unspeakable things to her. Things she was glad she could not see and yet could still feel them even when they finished with her for the night.
Unknown to the girl, the men had came upon a tavern on the road heading north to Tousir (City), they had left her in the cage, a cage no bigger than her actual body and leaving her sat down and cramped. A thick blanket thrown over the top slightly revealed her to the world.
The pale white skin hinted with a blue-purple. The long ears, red eyes and white hair. She was an unknown, nothing anyone had ever seen before on the surface. The Yaralti were unknown and only by accident had these bandits and slavers come into possession of the girl. Inside they partied away, drinking and feasting; leaving the poor girl outside in the cold of winter.
Alynae was rescued by a travelling bard named "Shadow". Breaking into the cage after putting the bandits to sleep thanks to his skill in poisons; the bard took the frightened and blind Alynae in to the tavern. He washed her up and fed her, giving some of his clothes for her to wear.
However not was all that it seemed. After that they proceeded to one of Shadow's hideouts.
Deep in the mountain forests of The Principality of Adestein's South region, they arrived at The Burrow, an old fortress left over from The First Principality War. Here Alynae began to learn several new tricks; travelling and navigating here on the surface, hunting, thievery and love.
She fell in love with her new protector. The blind girl had never loved anyone like this and he seemed to love her too. They shared her first time together and continued their relationship and tutelage.

Found during a storm outside The Monastery of the Atiporith by one of the Monks, Ashta grew up not knowing her race or her home. After 16 years of living at the monastery, she began to show an nack for the darker and more emotional sides to the Aether and was banished after an attack in which she slaughtered the bandits raiding their home.
Not far from the place she had lived for all her life, the monk was caught by Slavers and sold into Slavery. Soon bought as a new slave for The Ring-Dang-Do at the price of Fifty-Five thousand Crowns, the most famous house of Entertainment and pleasure in The Principality of Adestein's capital, the girl soon rose from Back girl to Front girl and would soon run the establishment with her husband. Although she would have to earn back her fee with the deal given to all slaves bought by The Ring-Dang-Do; “Earn your price thousand fold and you are free.”
Ashta would need to earn herself 55 million Crown to earn her freedom.
Ashta is a Ikini, a species characterized by their head-tails. She has orange skin with white facial markings, and her head-tails are striped with blue and white. Ashta's eyes are blue, and she has a strong and determined expression.
Ashta is known for her independence and strong-willed nature. Even as a young trainee, she often displayed a determination to prove herself and make her own choices. Ashta is a highly skilled combatant with her swords.
Ashta cares deeply for others, and her compassion is evident in her interactions with friends, allies, and even adversaries. Ashta is loyal to her friends and allies, forming strong bonds, her loyalty is a defining trait, and she is willing to take risks to protect those she cares about.

Born in the village of Nyborg on the southern Ablos (Continent) island of Alapori (Island), Astrid was the only child to Juuso Lytingdottir and Elina Lytingdottir. Both her parents died when she was young to a plague that ran through Alapori (Island), leaving her living alone in her Nyborg.
Her dream was to become a Shield-Maiden, a warrior woman of the Ablos (Continent) people, unfortunatly several villages of Alapori (Island) banned women from becoming warriors; keeping them to working at home while the men raided.
She was going to become the first Shield-Maiden of Nyborg's long history.
And so when Jarl Viljo decided to raid the Fae Monastary of Feslios, she snuck herself aboard the Long-Ship and headed to battle.
With the vivid blonde hair of her mother, Astrid's cheeks sun kissed cheek were lined with faint freckles and her teeth had a slight parting at the centre pair. Standing at 5ft 4", the girl stood with broad shoulders of her father and although in her younger years a flatter chest; this allowed her to sneak aboard the Long-Ship on her first raid.
Spunky and never letting things get to her, Astrid would much rather fight her way out of a situation before letting it get to her. Most of the time the girl did not think things through first but learnt that lesson on her first raid.

Brunhilde is a young woman with a slender and athletic build. She has long, white hair and striking green eyes. Her facial features are sharp and determined, reflecting her resilient and capable nature. Brunhilde often wears practical and stylish clothing suitable for her adventures, including a combination of leather armor and cloth.
Brunhilde is fiercely independent and determined. She has a strong will and is determined to shape her own destiny, resisting being controlled by external forces. Brunhilde is a highly skilled swordswoman. Her combat prowess, agility, and proficiency with a sword make her a formidable force on the battlefield.

Daughter to a whore, Brunhilde grew up in the small village of Großenfeld within The Principality of Arnvoren With her mother not really knowing who her father was, Brunny's life was one of dodging molesters and forced work in the brothel. She had decided long ago that she was going to kill the man who brought her into this world and the only thing that she had a lead to was the name "The Silver Stallions" and a sword.
Her father had been such a cheapskate that he had gone to a brothel without anything to pay the girls for his time. He had instead left one of his swords as payment. Brunhilde found out that The Silver Stallions were a rather strong and well known mercenary company in the north and would go north to find them.
At the age of fourteen, she left the brothel, carrying the sword that was as big as her, and set out to find and murder her father.

Colonel Hildegunde is a decorated soldier of the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation), known for her exceptional tactical acumen and ruthless efficiency on the battlefield. Despite her youthful appearance, being only 14 years old, she is one of the Imperium’s most formidable military assets, embodying a disciplined, pragmatic, and often ruthless approach to warfare.
Hildegunde was inducted into the Ilmarian military at an early age, quickly rising through the ranks due to her prodigious combat abilities and strategic brilliance. Her talent in both magical and conventional warfare has made her a legend among her peers, though many outsiders underestimate her due to her childlike appearance.
As one of the Imperium’s finest soldiers, Hildegunde is frequently deployed in key military operations, serving as both a frontline officer and a symbol of Ilmarian might. While her expertise lies in battle, she is sometimes assigned to diplomatic missions as a show of strength—despite her personal disdain for politics.
Hildegunde is calculating, disciplined, and unwaveringly loyal to the Imperium. She harbours a deep cynicism toward diplomacy, believing in the superiority of military force as the ultimate tool of statecraft. Her demeanour is cold and professional, but those who cross her soon learn that her appearance belies the lethal efficiency of a hardened soldier.

Lorenza de Calis is the protagonist of 5. Books/Non-Published/Novel/Noble Blood, Tainted Hands (Novel), a dark crime thriller set in the sprawling industrial city of Ilmaria (City). A former junior constable from a prestigious military family, Lorenza’s journey is one of betrayal, survival, and vengeance.
Disowned by her family for choosing the constabulary over a military career, Lorenza is assigned to a cold missing-persons case that leads her to uncover a sinister syndicate trafficking the city's poor. Her investigation results in a disastrous raid, ending in the massacre of her unit and her own abduction by the syndicate. Held captive and drugged with "Dust," a substance that binds its victims in dependency, Lorenza becomes a sex slave for the group. Despite their efforts to break her spirit, she resists, ultimately manipulating a younger member into falling in love with her. In a desperate act of cunning and brutality, she convinces him that she is his girl and eventually murders him and escapes.
Upon her return, Lorenza is treated as a pariah. The Constabulary blames her for the raid's failure, accusing her of collusion with The Syndicate. Her family casts her out permanently, ashamed of her captivity and what they see as her complicity.
Left with nothing but her resolve, Lorenza becomes a vigilante, systematically dismantling the syndicate that destroyed her life. Her crusade leads her to the remnants of the criminal empire, now fractured and controlled by Marcellan, a charismatic but ruthless new leader. Gaining his trust, she embeds herself in his organization, walking a fine line between ally and adversary. Along the way, she discovers the old syndicate was funded and controlled by Ilmaria’s elite, including the city’s Prince.
Lorenza’s journey is one of survival, justice, and moral ambiguity as she confronts not only the criminals who wronged her but the corruption at the heart of the society she once swore to protect.

Infobox
One of two protagonists in the short story "The Seeds of Beauvon (Short Story)"
Thylaise is a green skinned and red haired dryad girl with yellow eyes. Most of the time the girl wanders around naked due to the culture of the Dryad's of The Beauvon Wood distaining anything made of natural materials. The only things they use are gifts from the forest.

Silas Hulins
Brought up in The Beauvon Wood on the eastern coast of the Atilisle River; a river that flowed into the Tillcaster River along with the Reidmeny River and the Onoway River, TThylaise nin s'o cima, Murah ve s'o uh'el tan was once a human girl in one of the many villages bordering The Beauvon Wood.
Roughly translated from ancient Üstün means "Thyliase of the grass, Murah and the beautiful Dawn (Month)."
Alheit Aichhalden was the name of the girl whom were taken by the Dryads of The Beauvon Wood. Stolen while playing in the fields, she got too close to the Wood and was snatched up. Transformed into a Dryad at the young age of six, she grew up within the Wood
That was until she met Silas Hulins. Injured in a battle, Silas was found by the young Thyliase while on her Pilgrimage, a six year venture of solitude in the Wood as she became an adult.
Taking care of the human boy, Thyliase had plans to kill him, as humans in the wood was forbidden yet she was too young to be allowed to kill so deciding to take care of the human until she finished her Pilgrimage and would be allowed by her culture to kill him.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Adelheid am Tor, known quietly as Adel and on the streets as Del, is a professional thief who survives by understanding how people look past her. Living in a Tousir (City) shaped by stone gates, narrow laws, and rigid assumptions, she uses her visible disability as both shield and key. To guards, she is a nuisance at worst and an object of pity at best. To Adelheid, that blind spot is profit.
She moves between churches, markets, and gatehouses in an unassuming wooden wheelchair, allowing others to lift, push, or escort her where she is not meant to go. Coins, keys, seals, and secrets pass through her hands unnoticed. When subtlety fails or escape becomes necessary, she reveals the truth few ever see: a hidden mechanical, enchanted chair capable of climbing walls, racing rooftops, and vanishing vertically into the city itself.
Adelheid does not steal for spectacle. She steals because she can, because she is good at it, and because the world has already decided what she is allowed to be.
Adelheid is a woman of soft, forgettable beauty. Brown hair is usually worn braided and pinned to one side, practical and modest, often partially hidden beneath a shawl or hood. Her features are gentle rather than sharp, with thoughtful eyes that tend to look downward or aside, encouraging others to underestimate her awareness.
She dresses plainly in layered, well-kept clothing appropriate for a lower working class woman: wool skirts, simple boots, muted colours. Nothing about her appearance draws attention, and that is deliberate. Her hands are clean, steady, and far more confident than her posture suggests.
Her everyday wheelchair is wooden, scuffed, and visibly inconvenient, its wear carefully maintained to appear authentic. Only a handful of people have ever seen her other chair, a compact marvel of hidden joints, folded limbs, runic etchings, and quiet menace.
Adelheid is observant, patient, and quietly amused by the world around her. She listens more than she speaks and has learned that silence invites confession. Her humour is dry and rarely shared aloud, reserved for moments when she knows she is already winning.
She is not cruel, but she is pragmatic. Adelheid understands the difference between kindness and condescension and has little patience for the latter. She does not resent help, she simply charges for it without telling anyone.
Adelheid values autonomy above all else. She dislikes being owned, managed, or pitied, and her crimes are as much about control as they are about coin. She is loyal only when it suits her and careful never to owe more than she can afford.
Adelheid was born near the city gates, her family known simply as those who lived am Tor. Her condition was present from early childhood, and she learned quickly that survival depended on patience and adaptation rather than strength.
Her family scraped by on odd labour until illness and hunger claimed them one by one. Adelheid survived because neighbours helped her. Later, she survived because she learned how to guide that help exactly where she wanted it to go.
She began stealing small things first, food, coins, scraps of parchment. Over time, she learned routes, schedules, and the language of guards and clerks. The enchanted chair came later, commissioned in secrecy, built not to replace her chair but to give her a choice the world never offered.
Adelheid am Tor is no legend, no guild master, no whispered myth. That is her greatest protection. She is simply a woman by the gate.
And gates, after all, are meant to be passed through.

Adelheit is a half-human half-Vampire. She hides her race like the rest of her kind following the rules of The Brethren Accords.
Seen as a "Vegetarian Vampire", Adel does not consume blood from a living creature nor humanoid. She takes animal blood instead.
Adelheit is a slender teenage girl with bob-length dark blue hair that has long bangs that reach her chin covering the right side of her face and blue eyes. She appears to be a cute, normal girl that one would not suspect to be a vampire. She wears her waitress or high school uniform for work and school respectively, whereas her casual clothes are tomboyish streetwear.
Her waitress uniform is a white shirt rolled up to her elbows, a black vest, a red tie, and a black skirt down to her lower thighs. On top of that skirt, she also wears a brown skirt that reaches her upper thighs. She also wears tight red leggings.

#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Head of Bio-Neurological Systems Integration of Project Kriegerin and The Deep Crucible.
Dr. Alvra Keil is the cold, methodical architect behind the Kriegerin Project’s biotechnical core, personally responsible for designing both the biomechanical framework of the Kriegerin units and the engineered genome that became Brigitte Neuhauser. Equal parts genius and pragmatist, she views life, especially synthetic life, as a system to optimize, not protect.
As much closer as one could come to being Brigitte Neuhauser's Mother.
Dr. Alvra Keil presents a calm, clinical elegance that reflects both her intellect and detachment. Her ash-blonde hair is neatly cut to shoulder length, often pinned back or tied to keep from obscuring her face while she works. Thin-rimmed glasses perch perpetually on her nose—more a signature than a necessity—catching the sterile light of laboratory panels. Her attire is immaculate: tailored lab coats, pressed skirts or trousers, and high collars that lend her a severe, almost austere presence. Even her gestures are precise and economical, betraying a mind that wastes nothing, not even movement. In the dim light of the Deep Crucible, her pale complexion and measured poise give her an almost spectral quality—like something carved from glass and intellect, fragile only in appearance.
Alvra Keil is a scientist first, a human being second. Her intellect is extraordinary, but so is her emotional distance. To her, the human body is an instrument, the mind a machine of chemicals and impulses—beautiful in its design, but devoid of mystery. She speaks softly but with authority, her tone stripped of warmth yet laced with absolute conviction. Efficiency and order are her virtues; sentiment, a distraction. Though she rarely shows affection, her connection to Brigitte Neuhauser betrays a quiet, complicated tenderness—an unspoken maternal instinct she neither acknowledges nor understands. Beneath the veneer of professionalism lies a deep, private guilt for what she’s created and what she’s allowed to happen. To many, Alvra Keil is an enigma: a woman who gave life, but treats it like data; a creator haunted by her own creation.

Elira Voigt - Friend
Niklas Rosthagen - Ex Lover
Brigitte Neuhauser - Creator

Anya Volcheva is a young woman of the Alrussian Steppe village who becomes the first to offer aid to Doctor Dorian Viremont upon his arrival. Drawn to him by curiosity and a restless desire for something beyond the life she has always known, she quickly forms a close and increasingly personal attachment to the outsider physician.
Unlike the other villagers, who grow wary and fearful as the plague known as Krasnoglad spreads, Anya remains firmly at his side. To her, Dorian represents more than a man; he is a glimpse of a wider world, of change, movement, and possibility. This fascination evolves into a bold and unguarded affection, expressed through constant presence, probing questions, and an intimacy that often disregards social boundaries.
As fear takes hold of the village and suspicion turns toward the "Bachelor", Anya becomes both his strongest ally and a reflection of what is at stake; hope, youth, and the fragile belief that something better lies beyond the Steppe.
Anya is 18 years old during the events of The Red Hunger, with a youthful, energetic presence that stands in contrast to the weary stillness of the village around her.
Hair: Striking red, rare for the region, usually loose or hastily tied back, often tangled by the wind
Eyes: Light in colour, green, bright and alert, rarely still
Build: Slight and wiry, shaped by labour rather than delicacy
Her clothing is typical of the village, though worn with a certain carelessness:
Layered skirts and a simple blouse, practical but often unevenly arranged
A shawl she frequently adjusts, though it rarely stays in place for long
Boots worn from use, suited to the harsh ground of the Steppe
There is little refinement in her appearance, but a natural vitality that makes her stand out — not polished, but vividly alive.
Anya is driven by a deep, often unspoken restlessness. She has spent her life in a place where little changes, and the arrival of the Bachelor ignites something in her that had long been dormant.
At her core, she is:
Curious, constantly questioning, eager to learn about the world beyond the village
Impulsive, acting on feeling rather than careful thought
Open and expressive, unafraid to speak, laugh, or draw close
Her fascination with Dorian is rooted not only in attraction, but in what he represents. She sees in him a life she has never had , one of movement, knowledge, and possibility. This leads her to behave in ways that may seem forward or improper by village standards, though to her they feel entirely natural.
She is not naïve, but she is inexperienced. The realities of danger, illness, and consequence are understood only in part, and often overshadowed by her optimism and desire to believe in something better.
As the plague worsens, her defining traits are tested. Whether she clings to hope, adapts to the growing darkness, or becomes consumed by it shapes her role in the unfolding events.
The central figure in Anya’s world. She is drawn to him immediately, fascinated by his knowledge, his manner, and the life he represents. Her feelings evolve quickly from curiosity to attachment, expressed through constant presence and increasing intimacy.
To Anya, Dorian is not just a man, but a doorway to something greater. She trusts him even as the village turns against him, often placing herself between him and suspicion. Her belief in him is unwavering, though it may not always be fully understood even by herself.
Anya’s relationship with the rest of the village is complicated. She belongs to it, yet feels constrained by it. The traditions, fears, and expectations of village life stand in opposition to her desire for change.
As the plague spreads and tensions rise, this divide becomes more pronounced. Where others see danger and blame, Anya sees possibility — a difference that isolates her as much as it defines her.

Once a simple girl to a simple family, Arlayna was caught up in a Goblin raid of her family's caravan, with her mother, father, sisters and brothers killed and sodomised, the girl was quickly taken by the goblins as their next toy. However a passing caravan interrupted the goblins fun, ending in the girls throat being slit by the goblins before they fled.
With medical treatment she hung onto life and with the help of a mysterious Witch in the Woods, the girl was given an elixar to heal her wound, this however had a catch.
Her body began to rot, her skin turned palid and it was evident that she was dying; her brain and soul still intact, the girl had become what Lich's and Necromancers had been trying to do for eons, an undead body with its soul intact.
Being stiched back together with fresh parts, the girl now a walking corpse, tried to keep her life together.

#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Commander of Tier Theta Field Operations of Project Kriegerin and The Deep Crucible, Elira always looked one part drill instructor and one part off-duty party girl. Her black field jacket hung half-zipped, and the cigarette tucked behind her ear was, as always, unlit and entirely ceremonial—smoking was prohibited at this depth.
Elira Voigt carries herself with the confidence of someone who has seen too much and still manages to look effortlessly in control. Her dark hair, usually tied into a loose, practical ponytail, frames sharp, knowing eyes that seem to miss nothing. Faint lines at their corners hint at long nights spent staring at monitors and longer ones staring into the bottom of a glass. She favours a blend of military precision and casual disregard—her black field jacket perpetually half-zipped over a fitted undershirt, sleeves rolled to the elbow, dog tags clinking softly when she moves. Combat trousers and worn boots complete the look, though she often adds small, almost rebellious touches: a splash of nail varnish, a pendant from a forgotten lover, or the ever-present unlit cigarette tucked behind her ear. Even when standing among soldiers or scientists, Elira stands out—equal parts authority and recklessness, discipline wrapped in defiance.
Elira Voigt is the embodiment of contradiction—charismatic yet jaded, disciplined yet impulsive, professional yet deeply human. She commands respect not through rank alone but through the sheer force of her presence. Beneath the sharp wit and biting sarcasm lies a mind honed for tactical brilliance; she reads people and situations with unnerving speed. Off duty, she can be warm, flirtatious, even playful—sharing drinks and crude jokes to break the unbearable tension that comes with life in The Crucible. Yet there’s a haunted edge to her laughter, a weight behind her easy charm. Those who work under her know she carries ghosts—losses she doesn’t speak of, and fears she buries beneath bravado and control. In crisis, she’s fearless; in quiet moments, she’s fragile. Elira Voigt is the kind of leader who’d die for her team without hesitation—and drown her grief in whisky before morning.

Alvra Keil - Friend
Niklas Rosthagen - Ex Lover
Brigitte Neuhauser - Boss

A Druid of the 'Druid's Circle Commune, she left home on her Pilgrimage to find her mastery. Unfortunately, she has a problem with alcohol and the moment she drinks any, she's intoxicated. Her sober self is celibate, a vegetarian and soft spoken but closed off. Her drunk self eats meat freely, will have sex with anything and everything and is loud and outspoken on every topic.
Ellie is a half-elven woman standing about 5'4" tall, with fair skin, green eyes and long red hair. She has freckles on her nose and cheeks.
Ellie is shy and very socially inept. This makes it difficult for her to persuade others to help her and her friends out in many situations. However, she also has a strong moral compass, which leads her to question at times some of the rather extreme choices that her friends tends to make.
Although she has slowly been overcoming her own social flaws, at times her anger gets the better of her. She has been gaining more confidence in herself, and becoming more pragmatic, without compromising her morals. At times, Ellie is prone to acting impulsively, which has led to unfavourable outcomes.
However, she's also very tenacious and stubborn, refusing to give up even in the bleakest of circumstances and always wanting to go the extra mile to help others. Another thing that defines Ellie is her tendency to feel guilty. She tends to focus more on her mistakes than her successes.

Druid's Circle Commune

Infobox
Esther Stahnke is a sharp-tongued, book-buried university student whose fascination with the esoteric borders on devotional. While most students unwind with cheap lager and late-night cinema, Esther prowls second-hand bookshops, abandoned railway tunnels, and forgotten Üstün ruins. She is obsessed with the darker fabric of Fera’s magic; ghosts, cursed artefacts, Aether-bleed incidents, and anything officially labelled “best left alone.”
Calm, deadpan, and permanently sleep-deprived, she speaks fluent sarcasm and has the social warmth of a crypt door; unless someone shares her passions, in which case she comes alive with startling intensity.
A slim girl with dark bags under her eyes, short dark blue/purple hair, round glasses perpetually sliding down her nose, and a wardrobe of black jumpers, occult jewellery, and worn combat boots.
Dry, sardonic wit
Quietly brave, almost to the point of foolishness
Obsessed with magical theory and forbidden texts
Often underestimated due to her small frame and soft voice
Keeps a journal that is equal parts research notes and morbid poetry
Strong theoretical knowledge of necromancy, demonology, and Aether anomalies
Can recognise Üstün glyphwork at a glance
Remarkably intuitive with spirits, hauntings, and supernatural disturbances
Prone to getting herself involved in things sane people avoid

University Student (Occult Studies & Comparative Mythology)
Born in the outskirts of Ilmaria’s capital, Esther grew up above her grandmother’s antique shop; a cluttered labyrinth of cursed trinkets, creaking dolls, and Üstün relics brought in by collectors who didn't understand what they were selling. Her fascination with the uncanny began early, and by nine year old she was practising minor protective wards and ghost-luring rites in abandoned parks.
She intends to write her thesis on “interdimensional bleed phenomena and the metaphysical ecology of urban spirits.” Her professor is already dreading it.

Infobox
Gillian “Ginny” Ruggenale is a Human adventurer and scholar from the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation), best known for her daring expeditions into the unexplored regions of Fera. A gifted linguist and a dedicated student of Ancient History at The Tousir Imperial Academy she has built an academic reputation balanced precariously atop fieldwork that most historians would never dare attempt. Fluent in numerous tongues, including the lost and difficult Üstün language, Gillian specialises in deciphering forgotten cultures, mapping ruins, and uncovering artefacts tied to the earliest civilisations of the world.
Despite her academic background, Gillian is far from a sheltered scholar. She is physically capable, sharp-witted, and notoriously stubborn, with a tendency to charge headlong into danger when the promise of ancient knowledge is at stake. Her expeditions have taken her from Ilmaria (Continent)’s libraries to the jungles of Pawhye (Continent), to the stone halls of Dwarven keeps and the long-buried temples of forgotten races. Though still officially a university student, Gillian has already become a figure of interest to explorers, mercenaries, and scholars alike, some seeking her expertise, others seeking to prevent her from unearthing truths best left hidden.
Gillian Ruggenale cuts the figure of a field scholar rather than a classroom academic. Lean, athletic, and hardened by months spent trekking through jungles, deserts, and ruins, she carries herself with a quiet confidence born of experience. Her skin is sun-touched from long days under foreign skies, and faint scars along her arms and shoulders hint at close encounters with traps, beasts, and the occasional collapsing corridor.
Her dark brown hair is usually tied back in a loose, practical tail or bun, though stray strands inevitably fall across her face during expeditions. Sharp green eyes, alert, curious, and seldom still, miss little in her surroundings, giving her a perpetually assessing look. She dresses in durable, fitted expedition gear: sleeveless tops, reinforced trousers, fingerless gloves, and a weathered utility belt laden with tools, notebooks, and translation slates. A single strap of her satchel or climbing harness is almost always slung across her chest, part of her silhouette as much as any weapon she carries.
Around her neck she wears a simple green pendant, an old charm gifted by her mother when she first enrolled at The Tousir Imperial Academy. Though unassuming, Gillian treats it as a keepsake and rarely removes it.
Practical, rugged, and ready for movement at a moment’s notice, Gillian’s appearance reflects precisely what she is: an explorer who has lived far more in the field than the lecture hall.

The daughter to the chieftain of her tribe, The Serak Thaal, Göçebe lives in The Dread Valley (Region), and takes care of the various Automata that roam the valley. She is the direct descendant of one of the women who rose up against the ancient Üstün that ruled the Valley as their private reserve.
Göçebe is a young and agile woman with a strong and athletic build. She has vibrant red hair that is often braided, giving her a distinctive and practical look. Her facial features are determined, with piercing green eyes and freckles.
Göçebe's attire is crafted from materials found in the world and includes a tribal-style outfit made of animal hides and Automata's parts. She often wears a headpiece adorned with feathers, symbolizing her connection to the tribes in the game. Göçebe's overall appearance is a blend of resourcefulness, adaptability, and a connection to the natural world.
Göçebe possesses a resilient and inquisitive personality that defines her journey in the world. Driven by an unyielding determination to take care of the creatures dominating the landscape, Göçebe demonstrates a strong sense of justice, resourcefulness, and intelligence. Her independent spirit and empathy guide her interactions with the various tribes she encounters, as she strives to bridge gaps and forge alliances.

Born in Kokkan, Ike has no memory of her parents, she was taken as a slave by Umissian slavers and taken back to the Umissian homeland.
After escaping her captors, the girl now lives in the desert, alone and making do.
That was until she found a child, another Kokkan, whom she would name Su after the child's pointing at their chest and announcing "Su".
A Weilder of the Aether Blade known as Êtêr Kılıç.

Ike's Camp - Her home camp located inside an old sailing ship in the desert.
Gassam (City) - A Small Village in the desert close to where Ike set her camp.
Lazah Şehir (City) - The Underground city that Ike found Êtêr Kılıç and developed into a proper city with Ernst Kristoffersen
Ike has a distinctive and strong-willed appearance. She has hazel eyes and a fair complexion. Her hair, which she often wears in a practical style, is a brown colour. Ike's attire is often practical and reflects her scavenger background in the desert. She is initially seen wearing a beige and tan outfit with a distinctive head wrap.
