Isabella McLain is the daughter of Christian McLain, a businessman and merchant in the New World, living near Shade Cross, her father sold illegal goods to a local gang.
Isabella was the target of Solomon Sinclair's first robbery with the gang as bag-man; at aged 17, she was taken hostage by Solomon after the local gang intervened with their stage coach robbery.
This led the pair down a romance that would stay with Solomon until his death 2 decades later.

Christian McLain- Father
Annabella-Marie McLain - Mother

Shade Cross Region
At the age of 17, or just short of her 17th birthday, Isabella travelled with her father and mother in their stage coach, unaware that her father was using their journey as a cover for transporting illegal goods for a local gang.
During this journey, the stage coach was robbed by the The Van Der Graphe Gang led by Gideon Van der Graphe. This was where she was robbed by a 17 year old Solomon Sinclair. After the robbery was interrupted by a local gang interceding, Isabella was taken hostage by Solomon and the boy took the girl some distance away. After being shot twice, Solomon fell from his saddle.
Isabella gave quick medical aide to the wounded bandit. Deciding not to leave the boy to die, Isabella took Solomon to a nearby castle owned by her betrothed Phillip Heart.
Under her time with Solomon, she went by the name Jade Afton.

Infobox
Protagonist of the Novel Traitor In Love (Novel).
Julia is a Nu-Juren, a military created creature that can transform into a larger monster. She is sent as a spy into the Aplar Federal Republic (Nation)
Julia is a young girl of considerably short height with a small yet very muscular build and physique. She has moderately short blonde hair that is often tied at the back with her right fringe mainly draping over the right side of her face (though she tends to push it to the side on occasion, possibly for better visibility); currently she wears it down and it falls slightly below her neck. She has an oval-shaped face, blue eyes, a arched nose, and pale complexion.
Her hair is particularly pale and, when untied, reaches down the nape of her neck. Her eyes, although of considerable size and proportion, often have a sullen vibe to their appearance. Julia's casual attire mainly consists of a hooded sweatshirt of some kind underneath a jacket accompanied by dark grey pants.
Due to her harsh upbringing, Julia has become an isolated, exclusionary person; friendships do not come to her easily. She is rarely seen smiling and often has an emotionless expression. She is apathetic and somnolent, with little desire to put in any effort into meaningless disciplines or activities, and instead claims to focus exclusively on making it into the Constabulary to obtain an easy life.
While Julia tends to have a realistic outlook on life, she holds a fascination and even feelings of respect towards people who have a deep sense of duty and righteousness. People who devote their lives to and even die for causes they believe in.
Julia's sense of humor tends to be mocking, sarcastic, deadpan, and surprising. It also sometimes expresses a partial truth, and it happens mostly in intense situations. Despite Julia's usually cold and calm demeanor, she is capable of expressing her feelings in various ways. At the times she does lose her composure, she usually reacts with violence.
While outwardly callous, Julia has expressed levels of guilt and shock. Julia is highly intelligent, able to think deeply about situations, and has shown considerable problem-solving ability and a quick wit. These personality traits, in conjunction with her calm attitude and analytical skills, make her a good tactician. She is extremely practical and self-aware, being honest about her strengths and weaknesses, and is rarely ever prone to self-deception or emotional mistakes.

Aplar Federal Republic (Nation)

Karlotta Schonbein is a formidable mercenary and second-in-command of the Maritime Mercantile Legion, a renowned mercenary company operating in the world of Fera. Influenced by her strict upbringing and military training, Karlotta is a disciplined, pragmatic leader who commands both respect and fear among her crew.
She serves aboard the company’s flagship, Stählerne Vorhut "Steel Vanguard", a massive, multi-purpose vessel. This ship functions as a cargo transporter, oceanic explorer, and icebreaker, capable of navigating any sea condition. Equipped with advanced submarines, the ship allows for deep-sea exploration and covert operations.
Karlotta is known for her tactical brilliance, unmatched combat skills, and a no-nonsense attitude. While fiercely loyal to her captain, she has an independent streak that drives her to question orders she finds reckless or inefficient. Her past remains shrouded in mystery, with rumours of her ties to old Ilmarian military factions circulating among the crew.
Driven by ambition, Karlotta seeks not only to protect the crew and expand the company’s reputation but also to carve out her own legacy on the unforgiving seas of Fera.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Lâmera is an ancient Üstün elf wandering a world that has outlived her memory. Millennia ago, she was known as Zühreya, a revolutionary who attempted to rise against the Üstün ruler Yilmazok Akar. For this, she was sentenced not to death, but to erasure.
A living punishment was grown into her brain — the Nâsûr of Remembrance, a parasitic organism whose tendrils lace through her neural pathways, consuming long-term memory and continuity of identity. It cannot be removed without killing her. She no longer knows her origins, her crime, or her importance.
She travels to relearn the world again and again, unaware she is walking the ruins of her own past.
Lâmera appears eternally youthful, her features fine and softly angular, marked by the distant beauty typical of the Üstün. Her hair is pale, almost silver-blonde, worn long and loose or tied simply to keep it from her eyes. Her gaze is calm but unfocused, as though always half a thought behind the present.
She dresses practically for travel — layered robes, muted colours, worn boots — favouring comfort and repetition over ornament. Old scars trace her body in places she does not remember being wounded. When tired or near ancient Üstün sites, she often touches her temples unconsciously.
There is nothing overtly regal about her, yet people sometimes mistake her for someone important without knowing why.
Quiet, observant, and patient, Lâmera moves through the world with a gentle detachment. She is polite and thoughtful, but struggles to form lasting emotional bonds, sensing — without understanding — that closeness comes at a cost.
She fixates on small, ordinary details: the taste of tea, the sound of rain on stone, the shape of handwriting. Routine comforts her. Repetition steadies her mind.
Despite her softness, she possesses a deep, instinctive resistance to cruelty and authority. She dislikes being ordered, flinches from overt symbols of power, and feels inexplicable unease when confronted with tyranny. When she speaks out or inspires others, it is often followed by exhaustion or pain she cannot explain.
She is not afraid of forgetting — only of hurting people she will not remember.

Yilmazok Akar - Former Üstün ruler and architect of her punishment. Lâmera does not remember him, but his name causes visceral discomfort, headaches, and dissociation.
Born an Üstün elf in an age of immortals, Zühreya lived for centuries as a scholar, organiser, and quiet leader. As Yilmazok Akar’s rule hardened into tyranny, she became a focal point for resistance, preserving memory, names, and injustices that others wished to bury.
Rather than execute her, Akar sentenced her to living erasure. The Nâsûr of Remembrance was grown within her brain, its tendrils spreading slowly until her continuity fractured. Her rebellion collapsed not through defeat, but through forgetting.
Civilisation fell. The Üstün vanished. The law that condemned her ceased to exist.
Now, known only as Lâmera, she walks a world that remembers her better than she remembers herself — carrying a punishment with no master, and a freedom she does not yet understand.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Luna is a stoic and enigmatic Lupir-type Chimerae known for her calm authority and unshakable composure. Once a feared enforcer within the city’s underworld, she now operates as an the head of her own Alrussian Mafia
Outside of her work, Luna is rarely seen without her immaculate black suit and tie, a visual echo of the discipline and pride she once held as a professional operative. She speaks little, moves with purpose, and commands respect through presence alone. Beneath her reserved surface lies a deep loyalty to those few she trusts, and a quiet, lingering grief for the life she was forced to abandon.
Luna possesses a striking, almost unnervingly composed appearance. Tall and lean, she carried herself with the quiet, rigid posture of someone raised in discipline rather than comfort. Her face was sharp and elegant, high cheekbones, a defined jawline, and dark, expressive eyes that rarely betrayed emotion.
Her most distinctive features were her natural wolf ears, tall and velvet-black, positioned neatly atop her head. They contrasted with her straight, midnight-black hair, which she kept long and meticulously maintained. Luna’s natural wolf tail matched, sleek and well-groomed, often swaying subtly behind her despite her otherwise motionless demeanour.
Luna’s typical attire consisted of an immaculate black tailored suit, fitted perfectly to her frame, paired with black gloves and polished shoes.
Her expression was almost always the same: cool, unreadable, and faintly severe. Even in casual settings, Luna exuded an aura of precision and quiet threat, a presence sharpened by her stillness and the way her gaze seemed to measure everyone and everything around her.
Luna is defined by her silence, discipline, and absolute emotional control. She speaks rarely and only when necessary, choosing her words with clinical precision. To most, she appears cold, unreadable, even intimidating, but beneath her stillness lies a slow-burning intensity that makes people instinctively wary of disappointing her.
She is naturally observant, reading body language and motives with uncanny accuracy. Luna’s gaze alone can feel like a warning. She carries herself with quiet authority; she does not need to raise her voice to command attention. Her calm is her most dangerous weapon, and she wields it effortlessly.
Luna has a deeply ingrained sense of loyalty, though she offers it to very few. She protects those she cares for with the same unshakable resolve she applies to her work, and betrayal, once earned, is met with a coldness more painful than anger.
Her humour is dry and rare. She is not unkind, but she is emotionally guarded to the point of seeming detached. Even in moments of vulnerability, Luna maintains a veneer of stoic composure, refusing to let others see her break.
Despite this, Luna is not unfeeling. She simply communicates her care through actions rather than words: staying late to help, standing watch without being asked, silently fixing a problem before anyone notices it existed.
Her past trauma has shaped her into someone who trusts slowly and forgives almost never, but who, once she chooses her people, stands with them even at her lowest.
Luna was born in Alrussia; though “born” is too generous a word for how her life began. Like many Chimerae children, she was abandoned at the gates of a state-run orphanage, left with no name, no record, and no one who cared whether she lived or died. The Alrussian system was notoriously cruel to her kind; Chimerae were treated as lesser, their animal traits used as justification for discrimination, beatings, and exploitation.
In the orphanage, Luna quickly learned the essential rule of survival: speak little, trust less, and never show weakness. Her wolf ears and tail, once symbols of natural identity, made her a target. She endured taunts, punishments, and the cold indifference of overseers who saw Chimerae children as defective stock.
But she was not entirely alone.
An older boy, another Chimerae, noticed her. He had survived longer than most, hardening into something fierce and stubborn. He shielded her when she was too small to defend herself, stole food when she was starving, and taught her how to fight before she was old enough to understand why she needed to. To Luna, he became a silent constant: a wall between her and the cruelty of the world.
They grew up together in that hostile place, bonded not by affection but by necessity and the unspoken pact of the abandoned. When they finally aged out of the system, they left as a pair and entered the underworld as equals; two orphans with nothing but grit and the will to carve space for themselves.
Luna rose quickly. Her ability to read danger, to stay calm under pressure, and to execute orders without hesitation attracted the attention of those who valued competence over bloodline. He rose with her, never seeking power, content to remain at her side as her shadow and right hand.
Together, they built their reputation: Luna the strategist with a stare that froze rooms; he the enforcer who ensured her word was final.
Their shared childhood forged a loyalty that nothing; not violence, betrayal, nor the years of hardship, could sever. Even after Luna was nearly killed, maimed, and rebuilt with augments, he stayed. He is one of the very few who remembers the small, starving girl she once was, and the only one she has ever allowed to stay that close.

#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Maribel Corvin is an Ilmarian mercenary and fencer, conscripted from an orphanage in her early childhood and raised within the structures of a professional fighting company. Outwardly soft-spoken and youthful, she is known for her exceptional discipline with the blade and her unnerving calm in combat.
By 1600 E, Maribel serves as a trained infantry duellist within a mercenary army, operating during Ilmaria’s age of pikes, shot, and rapiers. Though still young, she has already earned a quiet reputation as a reliable and precise fighter, valued less for brute strength and more for control, timing, and endurance.
Maribel is a short, slender young woman with pale skin and natural red hair, usually worn tied back or braided to keep it clear of her face while fencing. Her features are soft and almost childlike, often leading others to underestimate her age and experience.
Her eyes are light-coloured and observant, frequently described as distant when she is thinking through footwork or measuring an opponent. Scars are minimal and well-hidden, a testament to her defensive style rather than a lack of combat.
She typically wears practical Ilmarian mercenary attire, favouring fitted doublets, gloves, and light armour that allows full freedom of movement. When off duty, her clothing remains modest and unadorned.
Maribel is quiet, reserved, and highly disciplined. Years of institutional upbringing have left her emotionally restrained, careful with words, and uncomfortable with overt displays of affection.
She possesses a strong sense of routine and control, finding comfort in repetition, drills, and the familiar rituals of fencing. While not outwardly aggressive, she shows little hesitation in violence when ordered or when survival demands it.
Despite her hardened upbringing, traces of gentleness remain. She shows particular kindness to children, the wounded, and those she sees as powerless, though she rarely speaks of her own past.
Nicknames reflect different sides of her character. Mari and Belly are remnants of her childhood, while Bell is used among fellow soldiers, a name earned rather than given.
Orphanage Wardens of Ilmaria
Figures who oversaw her early years and arranged her conscription. Their influence on her life remains unresolved.
Company Fencing Master
The unnamed instructor responsible for her early training, credited with recognising her aptitude for timing and defensive footwork.
Fellow Mercenaries
A rotating cast of soldiers who variously underestimate, rely upon, or quietly fear her composure in battle.
Ilmarian Orphanage District
Where Maribel spent her earliest years before conscription.
Mercenary Training Yards
Drill grounds where she learned fencing, formation fighting, and discipline from childhood onward.
Ilmarian Campaign Routes
Roads, cities, and borderlands traversed during her service as a hired soldier.
Maribel Corvin was born around 1584 in Ilmaria, though the circumstances of her birth and parentage are unknown. She was raised in an orphanage until she was conscripted into a mercenary force during a period of increased military demand.
Identified early as physically slight but mentally focused, she was assigned to fencing and duelling training rather than heavy infantry. Her childhood was dominated by drills, sparring, and instruction, leaving little room for a conventional upbringing.
By her mid-teens, Maribel was already participating in active campaigns, serving as a light duellist and defensive specialist. Her survival is attributed to her caution, patience, and refusal to take unnecessary risks.
As of 1600 E, she remains in service, her future uncertain and her loyalty tied more to structure and survival than ideology.

From the gutters of Tousir (City), name means “little wonder.”
A young street urchin, once a child of the lower wards and old canals of Tousir (City), who discovered her Aetheric Resonance drew vermin to her. She could hear their thoughts, simple, flickering things about hunger, warmth, and danger, and learned to whisper back. Over the years, she became the The Ratspeaker", a girl the slums whispered about. To some she’s a saint of the lost; to others, a witch of plague.
Her talent is technically a branch of Empathic Thaumaturgy, a minor aether discipline that bonds with collective consciousness; in her case, the hive-mind of rats. However, she’s never been trained, and her other latent powers (probably rooted in deeper empathic manipulation or swarming magic) remain dormant or uncontrolled.

Wears patchwork layers; oversized coat, rat-nibbled shawl, boots scavenged from the dead.
Skin pale and thin from living underground; eyes glint faintly when she uses her power.
Rats often perch on her shoulders or coil around her arms; like living jewellery.
Carries a lantern powered by a small Aether crystal (her “heart light”), which draws her rats when lit.
Gentle, melancholic, often lonely. She sees beauty in things others call filth. Her rats are her family; she names them, talks to them, listens to them. Despite her eerie power, she’s deeply kind, often helping the homeless or orphaned.
She distrusts authority, especially the clergy or guilds who would label her “unclean.”

#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
An Enforcement officer and Detective in the Ceset Uniformed Coalition Collective (Nation), Nadiya is Transgender, formally a male called "Jack", Nadiya transitioned during her first two years at the Precinct.
Nadiya has a worn, hollow beauty shaped by exhaustion and purpose rather than vanity. Her most distinctive feature is her long, unkempt red hair, often tangled or hastily tied back, streaked with grease or dried rain. Her skin is pale and freckled, the complexion of someone who rarely sees sunlight but often stares down fluorescent tubes and flickering neon.
Dark circles haunt her eyes, which are a murky green-grey depending on the lighting, sharp and observant even when dulled by fatigue. Her expression tends to rest somewhere between neutral and mildly irritated, reflecting a life that expects disappointment. When she smiles, it's thin and humourless; when she frowns, it's barely different.
She dresses functionally, not fashionably. Faded work shirts with the top buttons undone, sleeves rolled past her elbows, paired with creased slacks and a beat-up long coat that has seen better decades. Scuffed boots and nicotine-stained fingers complete the look. The smell of smoke, damp concrete, and machine oil often clings to her clothes.
Nadiya rarely wears makeup. If she ever did, it’s long since washed away. Any jewellery she owns is tucked under her shirt, forgotten. There's a quiet intensity to the way she moves: not elegant, not aggressive, just efficient. Like someone always a few steps from collapse but refusing to fall.
Nadiya is a woman in quiet collapse; held together by instinct, routine, and a deep-seated refusal to stop. At first glance, she seems cold, disinterested, or bitter. In truth, she is simply exhausted: mentally, emotionally, and physically worn down by years of fighting systems too broken to repair and memories too heavy to carry.
She doesn't trust easily. Words come slow. She listens more than she speaks, and when she does speak, it's usually short, dry, and just sharp enough to remind you she's paying attention. Her humour is deadpan and laced with melancholy, often mistaken for sarcasm. She avoids unnecessary contact, both physical and emotional, and prefers silence to small talk. Eye contact is rare unless she’s interrogating someone or about to hit them.
Suffering from mental issues, Nadiya has several 'things' in her mind, part of her psyche and could be described as 'personalities' that she debates with.
Semiotic Dissent - Her urges to Debate and make intellectual discourse and nit-pick
Cognitive Acumen - Her urge to Analyses and piece things together

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Nerisai Tülverin is an Aşağı girl from the old noble line of House Tülverin, a family renowned for their immaculate manners and their deeply problematic opinions. Known for her porcelain-doll innocence and fluttery demeanour, she presents herself as a gentle scholar of natural philosophy and Üstün theology.
However, beneath her soft smile lies an unfiltered torrent of prejudice, spoken with such sweetness that listeners often need a moment to realise they have just been insulted. Nerisai does not believe she is racist; she believes she is simply stating the natural order of the world as any civilised Aşağı ought to know it.
She is both unintentionally hilarious and genuinely insufferable, making her one of the most memorable young nobles wandering Ilmaria in its middle ages.
Nerisai resembles a perfect illustration from a children’s fae-tale book:
long, pale-blonde hair tied in loose ribbons,
large, doe-like emerald eyes,
pale porcelain skin,
soft features that never seem capable of malice.
Her clothing is typically Aşağı noble fashion of the era: flowing layered gowns, light fabrics in pale greens, creams, and golds, embroidered with leaf motifs. She carries herself as if perpetually on the verge of attending a choir recital.
Her appearance gives no indication whatsoever that she is capable of saying, with genuine delight, phrases such as “How quaint of them, attempting agriculture with those little hands.”
Nerisai is the perfect storm of sweetness, grace, noble etiquette, and unexamined bigotry. She speaks softly, smiles constantly, and never raises her voice, even when delivering the most outrageous, long-winded commentary on “lesser peoples.”
She does not view herself as malicious; her racism is simply the “truth” she was raised with. When challenged, she appears genuinely confused, as if someone has questioned the colour of the sky.
Traits include:
Oblivious superiority delivered with kindness.
Flowery speech masking barbed insults.
Academic curiosity, especially in botany and magical fauna.
Innate cowardice, hidden behind aristocratic composure.
Terrible at recognising danger, especially when she offends dangerous creatures
To her credit, she is capable of empathy; she just has to be tricked into believing someone is “almost Aşağı”.

House Tülverin Elders: The source of her worldview; ancient, aloof Aşağı nobles who believe the world was nicer before everyone else was allowed in it.
Shadow - Her New Master.

Tülverin Estate; an elegant, secluded Aşağı manor filled with libraries, greenhouses, and judgemental relatives.
Born to the prestigious House Tülverin, Nerisai was raised in a bubble of courtly privilege and Aşağı-centric doctrine. Tutors praised her intelligence but never corrected her inherited biases; instead, they dressed them up as academic facts.
In her adolescence, she developed an interest in the outside world; particularly “creatures” (by which she means everyone who isn’t an Aşağı). This curiosity brought her into regular contact with non-Aşağı travellers, who have been subjected ever since to her gently spoken but devastatingly arrogant worldview.
Despite this, some find her weirdly endearing. She tries to help. She is earnest. She means well. And she makes no distinction between friend or foe: she insults everyone with equal grace.
After dungeon delving into some ruins, Nerisai ran into Shadow, a powerful assassin and mage. A Lord in his own right. Demonic and powerful. He did what no one had done before to the girl and made her responsible for her actions. Through sexual abuse and demeaning acts, Shadow made her submit to his will. Branding her with his mark and putting his 'mark' in her mind through lust powered sexual magic.
She was used in his dungeon and even spawned out an Imp child in his breeding rooms. Named Emp by Shadow, the Imp would follow her from now on. A stain on her honour.
Once suitably humbled and dominated, Shadow sent her out in the world as his servant. A puppet, a pet.
Nerisai wanted to rid herself of her new Master's control, so would get to work, in secret, to collect powers and knowledge that she could use to free herself from Shadow's clutches. She would use magic to seal her mind in two, or more, as her Master had a leash into her mind, she would create hosts that she could use and control in a way that he would not be able to track, using her split mind to hide her actions from him.
When she was ready, Nerisai declared her intentions. She announced herself as Gölşah, the Black Sovereign. One particular personality in her mind, the one who had taken all the power, was now ready to rule.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Anastasia "Nastya" Vasilyeva is a young woman hardened by loss and shaped by a turbulent, violent past in Alrussia (Continent). At just 14, she finds herself on the run after her family is violently wiped out by corrupt officials, leaving her with a burning thirst for revenge. She is fiercely independent, resourceful, and calculating, but beneath her tough exterior lies an intense emotional depth.
Drawing on the lessons of survival she's learned from street life, Nastya quickly adapts to the ruthless world around her. Though she initially struggles to navigate a world full of violence and betrayal, Nastya proves to be cunning and relentless, seeking justice for her family in a way that mirrors the cold precision of the mobster killers she learns from.
Despite the bitterness and anger in her heart, she holds onto a quiet desire for connection, forming fragile bonds with those who show her trust, loyalty, or compassion. Her thirst for vengeance drives her, but it is her underlying humanity that complicates her choices, pulling her back from total darkness.

Escaping the farm to go to the big city, the girl tried to fufil her dream of being an actress.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
A former journalist now turned a conscripted soldier for the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation). Josephine now works as an intelligence officer for the Special Branch
Josephine Auerswald carries the look of someone who has lived through too much, too young, weathered by war, sharpened by necessity, yet still marked by the softness of the life she once had.
She has short, wavy blonde hair, cut to a practical length but still falling in loose curls around her face. Her features are open and expressive, with a pale, fair complexion that shows every bruise, every sleepless night, and every hard decision. Her eyes are wide, intelligent, and quietly haunted, the gaze of a former journalist who has seen truth turned into ash.
She looks every inch the reluctant soldier turned intelligence officer: resourceful, battered, resilient, and still holding on to the spark that once made her a seeker of stories, long before the war made her part of one.
Josephine Auerswald embodies a complex blend of idealism, grit, and quiet defiance, traits born from her past life as a journalist and sharpened by the brutal reality of conscription into the The Friebruckian Invasion of The Three Kingdom's war.
At her core, Josephine is driven by truth. Even after being forced into service, she retains a reporter’s instinct: observe everything, question everything, and never take the official line at face value. She listens more than she speaks, storing details, patterns, and inconsistencies with the same precision others reserve for weapon drills. Her mind is always turning, connecting threads, reconstructing motives, seeking the story behind the orders.
Despite her sharp intellect, she is not cold. Josephine feels deeply, perhaps too deeply for a soldier. She is empathetic, quietly protective of those around her, especially conscripts like herself who never asked to play a part in a conflict spun by distant men. She holds a natural discomfort with hierarchy and blind obedience, often following rules only long enough to understand how to bend them.
War has changed her, though. She has learned to compartmentalise, to swallow her hesitation, to lie when she must. There is a hard edge developing beneath her gentleness, the pragmatic ruthlessness required of an intelligence officer. She hates it, hates how easily she can now justify deception or gather information that might condemn someone, but she does it because survival demands it.
Josephine is resourceful to a fault, stubborn when cornered, and capable of bursts of astonishing bravery when the situation calls for it. Fear rarely paralyses her; instead it sharpens her focus, the way it did when she chased dangerous stories back in Ilmaria’s city streets.
Still, the war weighs on her. There’s a quiet melancholy in her—an unspoken grief for the life she lost and the ideals she fears she’s betraying. Yet beneath that sorrow, something fiercer endures: a conviction that the truth matters, even now, especially now. It guides her, shapes her decisions, and keeps her humanity intact amid the machinery of conflict.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.title: Taldiira Rilynarn
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Nave Nalore was one of the most powerful city states of the Yaralti to ever exist, its city limits stretched for miles under the surface of Fera (Planet) and those above did had no idea of those that that lived below. Even the Dwarves knew little of the mysterious denizens of the Unter-land. They delved deep but not deep enough to reach the lands of the Yaralti.
It was said they had been there since time immemorial, but some said they were not as ancient as that. Some said they fought the ancient evils before the Üstün and some said they were Üstün now turned anew. All of it stories and rumours. Very few on the surface knew of the Yaralti and those that did knew of only those who had fled from their under-home.
In the grand city of Nave Nalore, Taldiira was the only child of the Rilynarn bloodline, her father and mother one of the most powerful members of an Inter-City State Trading Company. They had power, they had wealth but it was not enough for the young girl. She had just turned the age of womanhood and would be expected to bear children, to join the women of the Unter-Land to forever keep the lineage alive.
She did not want to.
The fun was not stopping just for her to spread her legs and shit out a child or three.
The first thing she had stole was a bun from a street vendor, it had been such a thrill and ever since the young age she had first stolen she and into her early teenage years she kept up the fun. Even when only a young girl and still was not yet of child bearing age but allowed some freedom, she crept into the city and became a thief of the night.
Her long years of work paid off and now she was known to the clans and guilds of the city but not as her real name Taldiira Rilynarn; that would be a problem for her 'real' life, but as "Jo'parmak".
"Black Finger."
With her long silvery white hair tied up in a high pony tail, the grey skinned girl sat in the back of a tavern on the docks of the Unterzee, the vast ocean under the ground.
She had a new job, a new customer.

Infobox
Zemfira is a 5 feet, 3 inches tall blue Siren with blue hair. She wears a pretty dress and has freckles. She wears a belt. She sometimes wore a ribbon tied around her left horn.
Zemfira is excitable and eager. According to some, everyone tells her that she is pure of virtue, worthwhile, and a creature of some repute. She delights in small acts of mischief and trickery and can be plied with offerings of pastries.
She keeps a sketchbook that she appears to use as a kind of pictorial journal. It is unclear to what extent her apparent personality traits are genuine. Zemfira grew up with wealth, on account of her mother being a highly sought-after courtesan. This is apparent when she inadvertently dismisses a friend after he tries to offer her money, and in how much she gives as tips. When Zemfira's mother responded to her request for additional funds, it was considerably less than Zemfira had asked for, and she began to hyperventilate.
Although initially it seemed as though Zemfira was trying to break free of the protection that had surrounded her for her entire life and become an independent woman, she later recognized that protection was a sign of love.

The leader of The Coterie
The Courtier is a powerful and ancient demon who presides over a shadowed pocket dimension known as the Masquerade, a realm of perpetual twilight and endless festivity. Within this surreal dominion, revellers dance beneath hanging lanterns and fractured mirrors, their faces hidden behind ornate masks; each mask concealing something far older and far less human.
The Courtier himself is both host and sovereign of this infernal gala. Cloaked in splendour and secrecy, he takes the form of a graceful noble, eternally masked and impossibly elegant. His voice is smooth and melodic, yet every word drips with temptation and veiled mockery. He rules the Coterie, a gathering of demons, spirits, and forsaken souls bound by oath, pleasure, or punishment to his endless masquerade.
The Coterie - Leader

In the ancient history of Fera, a single Human gained powers beyond comprehension. Becoming ever lasting, become an Eternal (Race). Now he wanders the world trying to fight evil. He fought the Üstün, he fought the Yaslan (Race). Legend says he was there for the birth of Fera
Through the years, he would be hurt, even killed. His body would transform and regenerate to a new form; this would take time and a lot of energy but he could be male or female but always human.


The constant eternity of fighting drove him to a point where he could not fight no more. He was tired, evil could not be ended. So he took his own life.

During the late years of the 1800's. He regenerated again.

#Character #FeraCharacter #Canon
Infobox
The Usta Zalim is an ancient, androgynous entity of immense power and mystery, regarded in scattered records as The Master or The Demon Master. Neither male nor female but both and neither simultaneously, the Usta Zalim embodies the paradox of existence itself — a being beyond mortal or divine classification. Their nature is one of constant change: the fusion of opposites, the annihilation of boundaries, and the perfection of contradiction.
Long erased from recorded history by the Üstün, the Usta Zalim once walked among mortals as an Umissian Kräl Şah, a sovereign said to have delved too deeply into forbidden rites. Their heresy — an attempt to unite the mortal and the divine within one body — led to their execution by the hero Yilmazok Akar. Yet death did not bind them. Through ritual, dream, and flesh, the Usta Zalim endured, transcending mortality and returning as a presence that inhabits minds, bodies, and desires.
Accounts of the Usta Zalim vary. Witnesses and cult inscriptions describe them as impossibly beautiful and terrible, appearing alternately male, female, or as a seamless blend of both. Their form shifts to reflect the innermost thoughts of those who perceive them — sometimes angelic, sometimes monstrous. Common features include black horns, pale or obsidian skin, and eyes burning with teal-blue light, though even these are inconsistent.

The adopted son to the Crowle family, Alphonse was never sure of his real mother and father, all that he knew was a barcode on his wrist.
Living in a poor family, Alphonse did his best to live his life, loving photography and hanging out with his friends, the boy soon fell in with a few people at school, realising one of them was none other than Gabriel Geiger, son to the Duke of [The Principality of Adestein]], Alphonse soon wanted to keep his friend safe; becoming his personal bodyguard, (In training ofcourse).
During his training he was found to be a Gunslinger, being inducted into the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation)'s Cabal of Gunslingers upon his training. Skilled with firearms in a magical way, the boy uses his powers to keep his friends safe but also show off to the ladies.
Alphonse is a young man with a lean and slightly athletic build. He has short blond hair and blue eyes. His hair is often messy, giving him a casual and carefree look. Alphonse is often seen wearing a black leather jacket with white and orange accents, paired with a graphic T-shirt and black pants.
He also wears a wristband on his left arm and has a camera strapped to his neck, emphasizing his passion for photography. Overall, Alphonse's appearance is characterized by a blend of modern, casual, and adventurous elements, reflecting his personality as an energetic and light-hearted member of the group.

Erdal Nadir, or "Eri" as some of his friends called him was an Elf, more precisely an Aşağı. A "Lower" Elf compared to the ancient Üstün Aşağı of ancient legend. He was lithe, tall and almost feminine in his appearance. This did not mean he wasn't strong or manly, in fact he was quite strong and had quite the attitude when pushed.
His long ears showed the Üstün heritage of the Aşağı, he must have had a long Üstün line that was only broken by some interbreeding with Humans. There was no dwarf in him, he knew that much, perhaps there was a little Orc in him which disgusted Erdal so much to think about.
If he'd been raped by an Orc or fell for an Orc he'd kill himself outright. Foul creatures.
Erdal had the same fond-ship for the other races as most Aşağı, even in this modern age of acceptance and unity, he hated Humans and Orcs, he tolerated the Dwarves, Gnomes, Halflings and Dragonkin. Although he hated the Humans, he put up with them enough, this was where his attitude usually kicked in.
He looked down on Humans a lot, saw himself better. Most teased him by calling him an Üstün King, or even more to tease him, an Üstün Temptress, the Üstün's powerful female Entitled (Class) whom were renown in history for their ability to fuck everything and anything.
City of Anderloon - Home town
Long black hair was pushed over to one side and fell down the right side of his face, hiding one of his brilliantly blue eyes. His eyes changed colour depending on his mood and feelings, blue was calm and relaxed, red was angry.

Returning from battle, Eryndor discovered a group of abandoned children struggling to survive in the ruins of a once-prosperous city. Struck by their plight and disillusioned by the horrors of war, Eryndor vowed to protect these children and offer them a new way of life. Over time, these children grew into a tightly knit community, adopting Eryndor’s values of discipline, unity, and self-reliance. From this humble beginning, The Children of the Abandoned emerged as a structured and enduring fellowship.

Johannes Happel was Prince Elect of The Principality of Laugstrond during the years of 1956 to 1990 before his resignation to his successor.
During his early years, 1928, there was an assassination attempt made against his father, then a Duke in the running for the Prince Elect of the Principality. Both he and his father were saved by a member of the The Imperial Office of Intelligence and Information and Special Branch officer, Pauwell Von Dietingen. Unfortunatly his mother was not able to be saved in time.
Several decades later, the pair would meet again on Wineday the 23rd of Heathswrath 1950 during a transit through the Imperium onboard the famous Intercontinental Railway to a secret meeting with an Alrussian Delegation attempting to stem an upcoming war during the The Second Cold War of the Three Kingdoms. Pauwell would be travelling on the the same carriage, retired from his work in the Special Branch and The Imperial Office of Intelligence and Information but still doing occasional work for them.
The locomotive was attacked by the Umissian Death Brigade, an assassin branch thought destroyed decades before, and actually the perpetrators of the initial assassination attempt against his father all those years ago.
Surviving the assassination attempt, Johannes would go on to the meeting and successfully avert the Cold War turning Hot.

Primary Protagonist of the short story A Chance Encounter ( Short Story).
A Runaway deserter from the Ilmarian Army, Jules Fitzgerald is a Gunslinger on the run.

The Front
Stormbury (City)

Fo Roundfor
At a young age, Jules was always interested in the military, fantasising about fighting and watching the parading military formations.
His father was had been an Officer in the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation) and his life was destined to be one too.
During his teenage years, Jules was recruited by a Spotter team for the Imperator's Special Selection Service. The newly formed Gunslinger Cabal, formed in the wake of the ascension of Imperator Andreas Vandersryke to the throne and a Gunslinger himself, found Jules to be exactly what they were looking for.
He had the gift, the abilities of a Gunslinger. After being put through Cabal training, he was sent to The Front at the age of 24 on his first campaign as part of the 125th Ilmarian Line of Foot or more commonly known by their nickname "The Black Legion".
It turns out that war was not exactly how he had imagined it and soon the horrors of war turned a once proud boy into a coward and deserter. Fleeing the battlefield and taking to the road. Jules would find himself travelling the length of the Imperium to return home; to admit to his family what he did and beg forgiveness.
Date: Swordsday the 49th of Windsend 1807
Arriving in the city of Stormbury (City), the Capital of The Principality of Stormbury, Jules had managed to sneak through the city gates and was planning on taking the locomotive to South; however he was identified by a Military Police officer and chased down.
During the chase, the Gunslinger ran into Fo Roundfor, a Kobold Post-keeper whom was on the run for crimes unknown to her. Escaping together into the sewers, Jules took pity on the small meek creature but knew he had to keep moving. He could not face the firing squad before apologising to his family.
Another attempt to leave the city put Jules in the sights of the cities newly formed Constabulary.
Captured and taken to the Constabulary station for holding, the Gunslinger thought it was over.
All until the little Kobold Post-Keeper snuck her way into the station and busted him out. The two escaped, with Jules killing several officers on his way out, before blending into the city.

#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
A Private Detective based in Ilmaria during the early 1900's.
Born in the grand capital of the Imperium in the year 1869, Ludwig Flügel had a long life of turmoil and pain. His father was a book keeper for a banking establishment of lesser note and worked well to keep his family well looked after, although this led to his death through his tireless overworking late nights at the bank and an unfortunate robbery that had been planned when no one was to be at the Bank in the early hours of the morning.
Ludwig's mother was taken to the Imperial Hospital for the Mentally Unstable after a breakdown and attempted murder-suicide of herself and her son, whom was only aged thirteen at the time.
Ludwig's schooling had been helped along by his fathers work and the young boy's enthusiasm for the book became one just like his fathers. Working to keep himself afloat, the boy offered his work as a book keeper and soon with the help of some of the Imperial Underworld had gained himself a reputation for able to work the books so that no one could ever decipher what was hidden and a knack for finding what was hidden in those that did not want to be found.
With this newfound cash flow Ludwig applied for a place at the The Tousir Imperial Academy and began his student life. There he fell in love with the Histories of the world and would spend his time diving into books.
That was until the Draft came, war was a constant thing in the Three Kingdoms, the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation) and the Alrussian Federation (Nation) had no less than 50 years between any war for the last six hundred years. A Draft always came in for a generation.
Serving on The Front, a vast series of defences and trenches between the two Empires, Ludwig went from rifleman to Order-Runner to Radio Operator. Once the rotations were done, he was offered a place upon the Merchant Detachment of the Military, working the radio's on the transport and military watercraft.
It was here that he gained his fear of water, after the merchant ship he was serving on was sunk and he was left adrift in the Shimmering Expanse, Ludwig was never the same. He had seen something, he told whomever would listen and they deemed that like his mother before him, stress had induced insanity upon him.
Returning from the war upon a medical discharge, Ludwig returned to work as a Professor at theThe Tousir Imperial Academy, where he studied that which he had seen. When his studies were becoming too problematic, the man's tenure as a Professor was ended and he needed to keep himself a float.
Working as a Private Eye, the now Detective Ludwig Flügel had given up all hope on ever solving what he had seen.
Arrived in a small village in 1911 (Moonday 1st Windsend)

It was on the border and outskirts of the Tillcaster River or more precisely the Atilisle River that flowed into the Tillcaster River along with the Reidmeny River and the Onoway River . The Beauvon Wood sat on its Eastern side and the battle had spilled into the woods. Silas had marched a long way to get there and into his first battle he had stood with the rest of his squad.
There he had been killed by The Knight of Dal-Harad, or would have been if he had not been found by the Dryad Thylaise nin s'o cima, Murah ve s'o uh'el tan, a dryad girl on her Pilgrimage.

"How do you differentiate between a coward and a patriot? The coward screams when going over, trying to scare the Ilmarian, when the patriot stays quiet knowing that his mere presence sends the Imperials running"
-Lieutenant Vadi Kzyrgo, 11th Line of Foot
Vadi Kzyrgo, also known as Lieutenant Vadi was an officer of the Alrussian 11th Line of Foot during the The First War of Alrussian Aggression He's mostly known for his deeds during the Great Retaliation Charge when he managed to take an Ilmarian trench with only the help of his colour bearer Stostky Pavtrov and fifteen other men from the 11th Line of Foot.
The charge ultimately resulted in an Ilmarian victory but not without the destruction of Trench 156 that was vital to the Ilmarian front due to how close it was to the Alrussian border at the time. For his actions during the charge, Vadi received the Cross of Saints although he never wore it during his time in the trenches as he feared It would get dirty and dishonour the medal which resulted in only a handful of people knowing that he had it in his possession.

The Front
Trench 156
Vadi is always wearing his Uniform M-04 and is rarely seen without it, it consists of a brown jacket with seven buttons and yellow sleeves. Under it, he wears a yellow shirt along with yellow pants that are tailored to cause the least amount of discomfort at all times, this is due to him and most soldiers being expected to live in their uniform during their stay on The Front.
On his feet are black shoes with short heels and socks that reach to his lower knees for warmth, as The Front get's cold during the night. It is especially rare to see him without his ammunition pouch and tricorne hat that seems to always accompany him wherever he goes, on the ammunition pouch is the symbol of the fifteenth Tsar, Nicolai Ystrof.
Around his stomach sits a belt that completes the look of his uniform as well as holds his jacket together.
In his belt, the Lieutenant is seen carrying a Flintlock pistol that he always has loaded to shoot any coward if the need arises, he also carries a standard-issue rapier that comes with the uniform. In the later part of his life, he also started carrying around a Tolokonsky Mk III Flintlock Rifle.
The lieutenant is almost always calm even in the direst combat situations, the truth is that he is freaking out just as much as other people if he is being shot at, but he has been trained in the Alrussian officer academy of Zetriski to never show any fear and to be an inspiration to the men, but the last part is sometimes hard for him due to his happy trigger finger. If there ever was a situation where Vadi showed his fear, they would surely make him resign. The few times that Vadi has been angry it's always been for good reason, such as when in the unlikely scenario when he has to cooperate with an elf or when people don't listen to him.
One thing that Vadi dislikes almost as much as cowardice is abhumans such as [Dwarves and Aşağı, especially Aşağı. He sees these beings as inferior and weak compared to human physiology. It does not help that he was betrayed by an elf during one of his missions to a crypt that was revealed under no-mans-land, in the crypt the Aşağı backstabbed him when he was fighting skeletons that guarded the crypt.

An Alrussian philosopher and creator of the Moltov's Principle.
Yuri Moltov possessed a commanding physical presence that mirrored the strength of his philosophical convictions. Standing at an above-average height for his time, he had a robust and well-built frame, carrying an air of both intellectual vigour and physical resilience. His broad shoulders and upright posture conveyed a sense of confidence and determination, a reflection of the resilience required to navigate the intricate societal and political landscapes of 19th-century Alrussia.
His facial features were characterized by a strong jawline, complemented by a well-groomed beard and moustache, which added to the gravitas of his appearance. Deep-set eyes, framed by expressive eyebrows, hinted at the profound contemplation that often occupied his thoughts. Though his gaze was intense, it also harboured a certain kindness, suggesting an empathetic connection with the human experience he sought to understand and illuminate through his philosophical inquiries.
Yuri Moltov's attire was a blend of traditional Alrussian garb and elements inspired by the evolving fashions of his time. A well-tailored, dark-coloured coat with intricate embroidery hinted at his cultural roots, while the occasional Western-style influence in his clothing underscored his openness to the intellectual currents sweeping across Europe.
His hands, weathered and marked by the ink of countless quills, were indicative of the laborious process of translating abstract thoughts into written words. Moltov's overall demeanour, a harmonious blend of strength and contemplation, served as a visual representation of the intricate balance he sought to advocate between the individual and the state within the confines of the Alrussian socio-political landscape.
Yuri Moltov, a prominent 19th-century philosopher in the backdrop of the Alrussian Federation (Nation), emerged as a profound thinker deeply influenced by the complex socio-political dynamics of his era. Born into a society characterized by autocracy and societal upheaval, Moltov's philosophical reflections were intricately woven into the fabric of his time.
With an astute mind and a contemplative spirit, Yuri Moltov delved into the metaphysical nuances of the human experience against the backdrop of the authoritarian regime. His philosophical works often carried a subtle critique of the prevailing political structures, yet he navigated these treacherous waters with a finesse that allowed his ideas to circulate within the intellectual circles of the time.
Moltov's writings reflected a fusion of traditional Alrussian spirituality and the burgeoning intellectual movements of the The Revolutionary Directorate of Friebruck (Nation) that were gradually influencing the Alrussian intelligentsia. He contemplated the relationship between the individual soul and the collective consciousness within the context of a society marked by strict hierarchies and the omnipresent power of the state.
In his treatises, Yuri Moltov championed the idea of a harmonious coexistence between the individual and the state, advocating for a synthesis of personal freedom and collective responsibility. His philosophical musings were often expressed through allegorical tales and poetic prose, drawing on the rich literary traditions of Alrussian literature.
Despite the challenges posed by censorship and political scrutiny, Moltov's influence grew among the intellectual elite, and his ideas subtly permeated the broader cultural landscape. His legacy, intertwined with the spirit of a changing Alrussian, left an indelible mark on the philosophical discourse of the time, inspiring subsequent generations to question the nature of authority, the individual's role in society, and the pursuit of a more harmonious existence within the complex tapestry of the Alrussian Federation (Nation).

Infobox
Doctor Dorian Viremont, often referred to simply as The Bacheolor, is an Ilmarian physician trained in formal Imperial medicine, he brings with him a rigid belief in reason, structure, observation and logic.
Dorian Viremont is a man in his late twenties to early thirties, bearing the composed and deliberate appearance of an educated Imperial professional.
Build: Lean and upright, with a posture that suggests discipline and control
Face: Pale, angular features with a sharp jawline and high cheekbones
Eyes: Dark and focused, often scanning rather than resting; observant to the point of intensity
Hair: Dark, kept relatively neat at first, though it becomes more dishevelled as conditions worsen
His attire sets him apart immediately from most:
A long, dark overcoat suited for travel but of noticeably finer make
Layered formal clothing beneath, practical but unmistakably urban in origin
Gloves, often worn even indoors, reinforcing both hygiene and distance
A worn but well-maintained medical bag, containing his instruments and notes
Dorian is defined by his devotion to logic and order, shaped by years of formal training and a belief that the world operates according to knowable principles.
At the outset, he is:
-Analytical and methodical, approaching every problem with structured reasoning
-Composed and controlled, rarely showing strong emotion
Confident, bordering on arrogant, accustomed to being correct, and to being listened to
He places little value in superstition, viewing local beliefs as obstacles rather than insights. Despite this, Dorian is not without compassion. His commitment to treating the sick is genuine, though often expressed through action rather than warmth. He struggles with interpersonal connection, tending towards detachment rather than empathy.

#Character #FeraCharacter #NPC
Infobox
Emp is the bastard child of a Breeding Imp of Shadow and Nerisai Tülverin. Conceived within Shadow’s domain during Nerisai’s period of captivity and coercion, Emp exists as both living proof of her subjugation and an unwanted tether binding her to her former master. Named by Shadow himself, the imp was forced upon Nerisai and thereafter followed her relentlessly, a reminder she could neither deny nor destroy without consequence.
Emp is a small, wiry imp with a lean, sinewed frame and elongated limbs that give it an unsettling, predatory grace. Its skin is leathery and dark, marked by faint ridges and scars that suggest infernal breeding rather than natural birth although its skin is a lot lighter than normal Imps, and its eyes, a vivid Green, matched its mothers. Long, hooked horns rise from its brow and curve backward, framing sharp, luminous eyes that glow faintly in low light.
Membranous wings sprout from its back, ragged at the edges yet strong enough for short, darting flights. A thin tail trails behind it, expressive and constantly in motion. Emp often carries scraps of parchment, trinkets, or tokens clutched possessively.
Emp is sly, observant, and unnervingly attentive. It speaks rarely unless prompted, preferring to watch and listen, filing away information for reasons that are not always clear. While it shows a warped loyalty to Shadow’s will, its attachment to Nerisai is more complex, a mixture of dependency, motherly need, and possessive fixation.
It delights in reminding Nerisai of her past humiliation, not out of malice alone, but because that memory defines its own existence. Despite this, Emp is not mindlessly cruel. It can be cunning, patient, and even protective in moments where its own survival aligns with hers. Its humour is dark and mocking, learned from the environment in which it was raised.

Nerisai Tülverin - Emp’s mother and unwilling anchor in the mortal world. To Emp, she is both origin and obligation, a figure it cannot abandon and will not let forget the circumstances of its birth.
Shadow - Emp’s progenitor and namer. A distant yet ever-present authority, whose influence lingers in Emp’s thoughts and instincts. Shadow is spoken of with reverence and fear, as both creator and master.
Emp was conceived within the depths of Shadow’s domain during Nerisai Tülverin’s captivity. The circumstances of his creation were deliberate rather than accidental, part of Shadow’s wider effort to break, humiliate, and bind Nerisai Tülverin to his will. The breeding chambers where Emp was spawned were designed to produce infernal servants loyal by origin, and Emp was named by Shadow as an act of ownership rather than parenthood.
Upon birth, Emp was marked as lesser even among imps. He was not raised for command or autonomy, but as a reminder made flesh. Shadow ensured that Emp was imprinted upon Nerisai Tülverin, compelled to follow her and remain in her presence. This binding was not born of affection, but of punishment. Wherever she was sent, Emp went with her, an unavoidable symbol of her subjugation.
When Shadow eventually released Nerisai Tülverin back into the wider world as his servant, Emp was sent with her. Shadow framed this as a gift, though both understood its true purpose. Emp acted as watcher, reminder, and living proof of ownership, carrying fragments of Shadow’s influence within his mind. Through Emp, Shadow could be assured that Nerisai Tülverin never fully escaped the consequences of her captivity.
Over time, as Nerisai Tülverin’s power grew and her identity began to fracture and reform, Emp’s role subtly shifted. Though still bound, the imp’s presence became less a tool of direct control and more an echo of a past that refused to remain buried. How this bond endures, warps, or is ultimately broken remains unresolved, especially as Nerisai Tülverin moves further from who she once was and closer to what she is becoming.

Born on Towerday the 17th of Harvest 1996 in the village of Kings March (Village), a small village set upon the point on the river where Imperator Andreas Vandersryke made camp before setting off to retake the city of Vandus (City) during The Night of Long Nights.
Ilyse was born on the same day as his Neighbour Aurelia Rouse and would spend their younger years inseperable. The two would become almost siblings as they played and hung out together along with their joint best friend Willow Lientzen
After the death of his parents, Ilyse had grown discontent with staying in his hometown and joined the Ilmarian Army. Exceeding all the high standards of the trainers, he rose quickly through the ranks.
After serving several tours on the demilitarized zone between Ilmaria and Alrussia; formerly known as "The Front", Ilyse was selected for specialist training. Trained as a pilot, explosives specialist and special operations; Ilyse joined the Ilmarian's Special Forces.
A number of years into his service with the 9th Special Detachment, Ilyse was selected as one of the first hundred subjects for Operation Able Sentry. Operation Able Sentry was a top secret project for the creation of a super soldier to fight and combat The Scourge called a Zruhir.
Out of the 100 initial test subjects, only 10 survived, Ilyse one of them.
And so from these 10 subjects, and with Operation Able Sentry deemed a failure due to the casualty rate, Operation Moonlight began.

Nomad had led a long and dangerous life until he got a job. Nomad took many different jobs, Bounty Hunting, Package Delivery and Guiding people through the Kuru Alanlar, the vast desert of Umissia (Continent).
The job, delivering a package. The problem was that he did not draw fast enough. They caught him before putting a bullet in his head.
Left for Dead, Nomad was found by a doctor while grave robbing for parts, brought back to the town of Desert Springs (Town). Weeks went by as he was was nursed back to health. When the town was attacked by Bandits, Nomad got out of his cot and rescued the town, but not before accidently killing an innocent woman held hostage. Now having to move on, Nomad seeks the one who put him in this position, the one who shot him in the head and to finish the job he signed on of delivering the package taken from him.

Desert Springs (Town) - Rescued and nursed back to health before defending from bandits.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Nomad is a man without a past, a wanderer without a home. When he wakes in the frozen remains of a battlefield, surrounded by the faceless dead, he has no name, no memories; only the instinct to move forward. His gas mask, cracked and bloodstained, hides the truth of what he once was. His body is a roadmap of old wounds, each scar a story he cannot remember.
The only clue to his existence is a photograph in his pocket, an image of a woman he feels deep love for, with words: "Return to us in the Power Plant." He does not question it. He does not hesitate. He walks because something within him compels him to.
But The Tract is a place where the past is never truly buried. The closer he gets to his destination, the more the fragments of his old life claw their way to the surface. Hallucinations? Memories? Echoes of something inhuman? He does not know.
All he knows is that he must keep moving.
Because he is Nomad, a man with no past, no future, only the path laid before him.

Protagonist of the Novel The Children of the Banquet (Novel).
Created by Vannozzo de Albrixis, Princeps is an Effigy, a man made Automata. He was created with clockwork mechanical parts but was supposed to be fitted with Aether crystals for power, however his created was killed before he could do that and he escaped the carnage of his father's lab.
Found in a sewer pit by Daddy D, Princeps was taken in to The Children of the Banquet, a collection of runaways, orphans and street children taken care by Daddy D and Momma M. Princeps would become one of their 'runners' during the time he acted as a thief for the group until he was handed over to Momma M's brothel.
After being spotted by a much higher criminal leader, he was taken in to a more expensive brothel. During one of these nights, he was beaten by the client and one of his defensive subroutines was activated. He killed the man as well as several guards of the brothel who tried to stop him.
Now on the run from the gangs of Altenkau (City)'s slums, Princeps attempts to find his way and find out what he really is, living in Hotel Das Letzte Asyl. He joins The Gentleman Bastards, having a minor relationship with Red Fox.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter #NPC
#Character #FeraCharacter #NPC
Infobox
Mysterious, charming, and morally ambiguous, Shadow is a wandering assassin, bard, and sorcerer whose past is cloaked in lies as much as illusion. Known only by his chosen alias, A self-proclaimed Siren, he travels the lands of Fera weaving stories, poisons, and blade-work in equal measure, trading favours and death in kind. Beneath the façade of the playful trickster lies a calculating and dangerous individual with a sharp tongue, sharper claws, and an uncanny ability to manipulate both minds and magic.
Shadow discovered Alynae Helviar by chance, though some suspect fate had more to do with it, finding her imprisoned and brutalised in a roadside slaver's cage. From that moment on, he became her rescuer, her mentor, her protector… and something far more complicated.
To his enemies, Shadow is a ghost; a name whispered before death, a smile glimpsed before the cut. To Alynae Helviar, he is the only anchor in a world that betrayed her. Whether his care for her is genuine or just another manipulation remains to be seen… but one thing is certain: he always gets what he wants.
Among his many servants and victims, none are quite as strange as Nerisai Tülverina; pampered noble Aşağı girl whose aristocratic arrogance met its match in Shadow’s cruelty. After breaking her mind and body, he remade her into a vessel of obedience, leaving behind a smiling, fractured puppet who now serves him in the world above… even as she secretly plots to one day be free.
Shadow is an effortlessly striking figure, both playful and sinister in equal measure. His skin is a deep crimson, offset by golden-yellow, predatory eyes that gleam with perpetual amusement. His face is youthful and handsome, almost charmingly mischievous, with sharp fangs that peek from his lips even when he's grinning sweetly, which is often.
Framing his face is a tousled mane of dark, ink-black hair with an almost metallic sheen, flowing down past his shoulders in waves that seem as untamed as his nature. Two straight, prominent horns rise from his brow, tapering to polished points. His long ears are sharp and expressive, always twitching at some unseen amusement.
He wears a deep green cloak or tunic depending on the day, always finely cut and decorated with stylised ties or embroidery that hint at a vanity lurking under his chaotic façade. On formal occasions, he dons a regal ensemble of gold-trimmed green velvet, adorned with belts and ornamental clasps, giving him the air of a bard-king, or a tyrant playing dress-up.
Shadow's tail is long and agile, with a spaded tip often seen curling or twitching like a cat mid-hunt. He moves with a dancer’s grace and a devil’s confidence, lounging with the entitlement of someone who has never once been told “no.”
Though short in stature compared to many warriors, he makes up for it in sheer presence. His posture, whether slouched across a throne with a lute or leaning in too close with a toothy smile, is always designed to unsettle.
"He has the look of a charming street rogue turned dungeon prince. The kind of man you’d regret sleeping with, assuming you survived the encounter."
Shadow is a master of contradiction: seductive yet cruel, playful yet calculated, charming yet utterly monstrous. He delights in games, especially the kind where only he knows the rules. Every word he speaks drips with flirtation or mockery, often both, and he enjoys unsettling others with his unnatural cheerfulness and smiling malice.
He considers himself an artist of control. To him, domination is a dance, and he prefers to lead with honeyed words and velvet chains rather than brute force, though he is fully capable of cruelty when denied what he wants. His sadism is rarely loud; it's theatrical, intimate, and always personal.
He is, above all, deeply narcissistic. Shadow believes himself to be a lord among lesser beings, and every act he commits is just another brushstroke in the masterpiece of his own legend. Yet he is not humourless, far from it. He laughs easily, often inappropriately, and treats the world like a stage built for his entertainment.
Despite this, he is dangerously intelligent and magically adept. Behind the lazy grin lies a meticulous mind that plans years ahead, keeping secrets within secrets and pawns within pawns. He can switch from laughter to ice in a heartbeat, his temper, when it shows, is cold, not hot.

Nerisai Tülverin - A once-proud Aşağı noble girl, now remade into Shadow’s servant and plaything. He broke her not with fire or chain, but with twisted affection and sexual domination. She is, to him, both an experiment and a trophy, proof that even the most delicate can be shattered beautifully. He refers to her with pet names ranging from “Sweetling” to “My Little Thorn.” Whether he truly cares or merely enjoys the game is unclear.
Alynae Helviar - A blind Yaralti girl whom Shadow found locked in a slaver's cage, starved, abused, and alone. What began as an impulsive rescue quickly turned into something deeper, darker, and far more complex. Shadow became her protector, teacher, and manipulator, guiding her hand as she took her first life, warming her body with magic, and reshaping her mind with charm and subtle sorcery. He calls her his apprentice, praises her obedience, and rewards her devotion with gifts, tenderness, and whispered lies. Whether he truly cares for her or merely enjoys possessing something so rare, broken, and powerful is unclear. But one thing is certain: Alynae believes she owes him everything and Shadow is more than happy to let her believe it.

The Protagonist of the novel series "The Dastardly Tales of the Van Der Graph Gang".

The Van Der Graphe Gang - Lead Enforcer
Solomon Sinclair was born in the The Three Kingdoms (Continent) nation of Ilmarian Imperium (Nation) to a man on the run and a prostitute. As a child he ran on the street and was the head of a small gang of pick pockets.
After some years he attempted to steal from a pair of men, these men were Gideon Van der Graphe and Elias Burress. These men were impressed by the young boy and after finding out that both his parents were dead, took it upon themselves to take him in. They taught him to read and write, to count and to work as an actual theif.
Eventually the Law caught up to the burgeoning The Van Der Graphe Gang and they fled across The Windergonie Domain, the ocean splitting The Three Kingdoms (Continent) and Pawhye (Continent). The three landed in Landfall and quickly set upon themselves to make a name for themselves.
The Van Der Graphe Gang slowly grew and as his place as the adopted son of the two founders, Solomon became the Lead Enforcer of the gang.
It was not until a heist that went wrong that Solomon found out he was even more special than he had assumed., A shotgun to the face resulted in the death of the shooter instead and in the stress of the moment Solomon had backfired the weapon with his hidden powers. Solomon was a Gunslinger, a special kind of mage who uses gunpowder and firearms.
Developing his skills over the years, Solomon became one of the best Gunslingers in Pawhye (Continent).
Usually armed with a pair of cartridge converted Darrington 1800 Cap & Ball Pistols and a Vanderbilt Lever Action Rifle, of which the latter was a precious gift from Gideon Van der Graphe on his 18th bithday.

Dressed in either leather or plate armour, Tazdu Varross; better known as The Stranger by most people and few by Quill is a perfect example of a member of 'The Children of the Abandoned'.
The key characteristic of a member of The Children of the Abandoned is their helmet. Most, if not all, wear a sealed helmet that completely hides their face from view, this helmet is kept on at all times and only removed for food, sleep or in a time and place where the wearer will be alone.
If the face is seen by anyone, it is a dishonour on the member and it cannot be replaced on the head.
Most helmets come as Armets or full face helms.
Quill is usually equipped with a longsword, a longbow, a Darrington 1814 Breach Loading Rifle and a set of Darrington 1800 Cap & Ball Pistol.
Quill has a stern temper and will. He is bound to his own code of honour and that of The Children of the Abandoned. He is loyal and knows when he must break the law to achieve what he needs.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
