#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Tsusgan Krovin is the current Haematurge of the Krovin bloodline, inheritor of a sacred tradition stretching back countless generations. Among his people, blood is not merely a fluid but the vessel of memory, ancestry, and identity. The Haematurge serves as physician, anatomist, spiritual guide, and keeper of lineage, entrusted with preserving both the bodies and histories of his kin.
Where Imperial doctors seek answers in books and laboratories, Tsusgan seeks them in flesh, bone, and blood. He believes that every wound tells a story, every scar carries meaning, and every life is connected to those who came before. Though respected by his people, many outsiders view him with suspicion, seeing his practices as primitive, unsettling, or dangerously close to sorcery.
As the Red Hunger spreads across the land, Tsusgan finds himself caught between the old world and the new, forced to confront horrors neither tradition nor science can fully explain.
Tsusgan is a broad-shouldered man in his early thirties, standing taller than most of his kin. Years spent handling carcasses, patients, and ritual work have given him powerful hands and a sturdy build rather than the refined appearance of an Imperial scholar.
His dark hair is worn long and tied behind his head, often braided with carved bone beads representing deceased ancestors of the Krovin line. His skin is weathered by wind and sun, and his dark eyes possess a quiet intensity that many find unsettling. They seem to study a person's veins and posture as much as their face.
His clothing combines practical steppe garments with ceremonial elements. Heavy leather coats, fur-lined collars, and layered robes are adorned with stitched patterns resembling veins and branching blood vessels. Around his neck hangs an ancestral knife used by generations of Haematurges, its handle polished smooth by centuries of use.
His hands are often stained by herbs, dyes, blood, or ink, and the scent of medicinal plants follows him wherever he goes.
Tsusgan is thoughtful, patient, and observant. He rarely speaks without purpose and prefers listening to others before offering his judgement.
Unlike many scholars, he possesses little arrogance. He respects knowledge regardless of its source, whether it comes from ancient tradition, common folk wisdom, or Imperial medicine. However, he becomes fiercely stubborn when he believes outsiders dismiss his people's traditions without understanding them.
He has a deep respect for life, but not a sentimental one. Years of witnessing birth, illness, slaughter, and death have taught him that all living things eventually return to the earth. As a result, he is unusually comfortable discussing mortality and often unnerves others with his calm acceptance of it.
Though outwardly composed, Tsusgan carries the weight of expectation. He is not merely a man but the latest bearer of an inherited duty. The fear of being the Krovin who fails his ancestors haunts him more than any personal danger.
An Imperial physician and scholar representing the growing influence of science and rationalism. The two men often clash philosophically, yet Tsusgan cannot deny Dorian's intelligence. Though they approach medicine from opposing directions, they occasionally arrive at the same conclusions.
Tsusgan views Dorian as both rival and potential ally.
The tribal leaders and spiritual authorities who safeguard the traditions of Tsusgan's people. They regard him as both servant and heir to ancient responsibilities.
Though long dead, Tsusgan considers the previous Haematurges among the most important influences in his life. Their journals, teachings, and preserved knowledge guide many of his decisions.
The previous Haematurge and Tsusgan's greatest teacher. Though deceased, his memory continues to shape Tsusgan's understanding of duty, sacrifice, and the meaning of blood.
The ancestral home of the Krovin line. Equal parts residence, clinic, archive, and shrine, it contains generations of anatomical studies, blood records, and sacred relics.
Ancient burial grounds of the Kin. Tsusgan frequently visits them to reflect, perform rituals, and consult ancestral traditions.
A bustling district where locals gather to trade livestock, medicines, herbs, and rumours. Tsusgan often learns more useful information here than from any official source.
Places where livestock are slaughtered and processed. To outsiders they are unpleasant workplaces; to Tsusgan they are classrooms where the truths of flesh and anatomy reveal themselves.
The vast ancestral homeland of his people. Tsusgan believes the land itself remembers those who have walked upon it and often seeks solitude there when troubled.
Tsusgan Krovin was born into one of the oldest and most respected bloodlines among the Kin. From childhood, it was understood that he would inherit the mantle of Haematurge from his father.
His education began long before he could read. He learned anatomy by helping butcher livestock, studied herbs alongside healers, and listened to ancestral teachings passed down through oral tradition. While other children played, Tsusgan was taught to recognise bones by touch, identify illnesses by scent, and understand the stories carried within scars and bloodlines.
As he grew older, his father introduced him to the secret knowledge of the Krovin line. He studied preserved journals written by generations of Haematurges and learned techniques considered strange or unsettling by outsiders.
When his father died, Tsusgan inherited not only the ancestral knife and title but also the immense responsibility that came with them.
For years he served his people faithfully, balancing medicine, ritual, and leadership. Yet the arrival of increasing Imperial influence challenged everything he had been taught. Scholars and physicians dismissed ancient practices as superstition, while many of his own people began embracing modern ideas.
Now, with the Red Hunger threatening the land, Tsusgan stands at a crossroads. The old knowledge alone may not be enough to save his people. Yet he fears that abandoning it entirely would mean losing something far more precious than life itself.
The blood remembers. The question is whether anyone still knows how to listen.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Asuka Kosuke appears to be an 18 year old boy of Kokkan origin. He has long black hair and a feminine featured body and face. Most of the time he could very easily pass for a female.
Asuka is a Rosutko, a "Lost Soul" in the Kokkan language.
Asuka : "Asu" means "to fly" and "Ka" means "bird"." "Asu" means "tomorrow" and "Ka" means "fragrance"
Kosuke : "Ko" means "peace" also "filial piety, obedience" or "Ko" means "prosperous" combined with "Suke" meaning "forerunner, herald."
An ancient set of scrolls passed through the ages tells a story. Here is a snippit of the scroll, translated into Ilmarian.
"It was to the Kosuke family that the world fell to. In their hands it burnt, it was raped, it was pillaged. The Kosuke came and went. The homeland burnt and all who rose up fell to the sword."
"One thousand came and rose against the flying bird who heralded peace. The Asuka Kosuke."
The art shows a thousand men fighting a single warrior, the warrior on the page was black and inked completely, no features. A demon with horns and wings
"The Flying Bird fell to a thousand swords but the thousands swords fel lto the flying bird. It was here the final peace occured The shards of the Flying Bird were sent far and wide, guarded by the Ko of the thousand swords, the spirits of the thousand warriors."

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Dorian Valcourt is an Ilmarian nobleman, scholar, and consulting investigator whose reputation has spread throughout the nation. Although frequently employed by the Interior Ministry, provincial constabularies, universities, and members of the aristocracy, he serves no institution directly and answers only to himself. Possessing a brilliant analytical mind and an obsessive devotion to evidence, Valcourt has solved murders, exposed conspiracies, dismantled criminal organisations, and uncovered political scandals that others considered unsolvable.
Unlike many scholars and occultists of his age, Valcourt neither dismisses nor embraces the supernatural. To him, all phenomena deserve investigation, regardless of how impossible they may appear. Whether faced with a serial killer, an ancient curse, a rogue Entitled, or rumours of forgotten gods, his response remains the same:
"Show me the evidence."
His growing career has drawn him into mysteries that challenge the foundations of reason itself, leading him towards truths buried beneath Ilmaria's history and beyond the limits of accepted magical theory.
Dorian stands at approximately six feet in height, possessing a lean, almost gaunt frame more suited to libraries than battlefields. Years spent studying by candlelight and travelling across crime scenes have left him pale, with sharp features and perpetually tired eyes.
His dark brown hair is usually unkempt, often appearing as though he has run his hands through it repeatedly while contemplating a problem. He maintains a neatly trimmed moustache and short beard, more out of habit than vanity.
His eyes are a striking grey-blue, known for making people feel as though they are being examined rather than spoken to.
He typically dresses in dark, tailored Ilmarian noble fashion:
Long wool overcoats
High-collared waistcoats
Fine leather gloves
Walking cane
Pocket watch
Spectacles used only for reading
He carries a leather notebook almost everywhere he goes, often jotting down observations in shorthand intelligible only to himself.
Many describe him as looking more like a professor than a detective.
Dorian is highly intelligent, observant, and relentlessly curious.
He possesses little patience for superstition, incompetence, or emotional reasoning, preferring evidence above all else. While not intentionally rude, he often forgets social niceties when focused on an investigation.

Exceptional deductive reasoning
Vast academic knowledge
Fearless pursuit of truth
Resistant to manipulation
Remarkably composed under pressure

Obsessive
Insomniac
Arrogant regarding his intellect
Neglectful of his own health
Struggles to empathise with others
Despite his detached nature, he is not cruel. He genuinely believes that understanding the truth is the greatest service one can provide to the living and the dead alike.
One of his greatest fears is not death.
It is uncertainty.
Dorian can tolerate danger.
He cannot tolerate not knowing.
Dorian's father and patriarch of House Valcourt.
A respected nobleman who expected his son to enter politics or government service. While proud of Dorian's accomplishments, he privately considers his son's profession beneath the dignity of their family.
Dorian's younger sister.
One of the few people capable of speaking candidly to him without receiving a cutting remark in return. She often worries about his isolation and unhealthy obsessions.
Senior Constabulary investigator.
Their relationship is complicated.
Kruger simultaneously respects, admires, and despises Dorian. He frequently requests Valcourt's assistance while resenting how often the nobleman solves cases that have frustrated official investigators for months.
Scholar of history and arcane studies.
One of Dorian's oldest acquaintances and a frequent source of information regarding ancient cultures, magical phenomena, and forgotten civilisations.
An unidentified individual repeatedly connected to several unrelated investigations.
Little is known about them beyond their apparent interest in collecting forbidden texts and occult knowledge. Dorian has encountered traces of their involvement in multiple cases over the years.
The ancestral estate of House Valcourt.
Located outside the Ilmarian capital, the manor serves as Dorian's legal residence, though he rarely spends time there.
Dorian's actual home.
An ageing noble townhouse within the capital city, filled with books, maps, case files, evidence lockers, and curiosities from countless investigations.
Most visitors describe it as organised chaos.
One of Dorian's most frequented locations.
Many of his investigations begin amongst forgotten records, shipping manifests, census rolls, and centuries-old documents.
A prestigious academic institution.
Its libraries and scholars provide valuable resources during particularly complex investigations.
The oldest district of the capital.
A maze of narrow streets, hidden courtyards, and ancient foundations dating back centuries. Numerous criminal organisations, secret societies, and strange rumours originate here.
Dorian Valcourt was born into House Valcourt, an old noble family whose influence stretched back centuries within Ilmaria. From a young age he displayed an unusual intellect, often spending more time studying maps, books, and records than participating in noble social functions.
His education was extensive and included:
History
Law
Natural philosophy
Magical theory
Linguistics
Forensic medicine
By his early twenties he had gained a reputation amongst academics for solving historical and legal disputes through meticulous research and logical analysis.
His first major investigation occurred when a series of murders baffled both local authorities and magical experts. Through careful examination of evidence overlooked by others, Dorian identified the culprit and exposed corruption within the investigation itself.
Word of his success spread rapidly.
Over the following decade he became increasingly sought after by government officials, nobles, and law enforcement agencies throughout Ilmaria.
Numerous high-profile cases followed:
The Blackwater Murders
The Ashford Poisonings
The Night Market Conspiracy
The Cathedral Theft
The Severed Hand Society
With each solved mystery, his reputation grew.
So too did the nature of the cases.
Simple murders became occult murders.
Occult murders became ancient mysteries.
Ancient mysteries became encounters with things that should not exist.
In recent years Dorian has found himself investigating a disturbing pattern. Across Ilmaria and beyond, unrelated incidents appear connected by recurring symbols, forgotten languages, impossible architecture, and references to entities absent from every known historical record.
For the first time in his life, Dorian Valcourt has begun to encounter mysteries for which reason alone may not be enough.
And that possibility frightens him more than any monster ever could.

#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
A Wayrider, his name, Hans von Fernweg, means, Hans "Of the Far Road." in the old tongue.
A wanderer, keeping to the roads armed with rapier, Flintlock rifle and musket and various scholarly affects.
His appearance is rugged and seasoned; a man weathered by countless miles, storms, and unseen dangers. He wears a dark forest-green cloak over worn leathers and wool, layered with traveling belts, satchels, and utility pouches. A rapier hangs from his belt, and his boots are scuffed with the dirt of a dozen nations.
His silver-streaked hair is swept back from a lined, stoic face. His eyes are grey and distant; always watching the path ahead, even when still. He bears the Split Road symbol carved on a silvert talisman at his neck and occasionally etched onto trees near crossroads, marking places where choices weigh heavy.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
Igor Dimitrov is a highly efficient and cold-hearted assassin, as well as a body disposal expert, working for the ruthless criminal syndicates that control Alrussia (Continent) in the 1990s. Born into the gritty streets of a war-torn Alrussian city bordering The Front, Igor was trained from a young age in the art of violence and discretion. His quiet demeanour and sharp instincts make him a trusted enforcer, capable of eliminating high-profile targets and disappearing without leaving a trace.
A man of few words, Igor specializes in making bodies vanish; no questions asked, catering to the mob's need for secrecy. His reputation is built on an unshakable professionalism that demands loyalty, yet there’s a darker side to his work: the toll it takes on his psyche. Despite his detachment from the world around him, Igor holds onto a quiet sense of honour, only intervening in matters when his morality outweighs his business. Deep down, he is a man trapped in his past, struggling to balance his humanity with the violent life he can never seem to escape.

Infobox “IMG” is not created yet. Click to create.
Once a firebrand preacher in the river-town of Caldrin’s Bluff, Josiah M'barek took up arms after a massacre at his mission chapel left twenty-seven innocents dead. Since then, he's wandered the deserts of Umissia, bearing scripture in one hand and a revolver in the other. Folks call him the Gunsaint—half myth, half man of God.
He preaches salvation, but offers no mercy to bandits, slavers, or those who prey on the weak. Stories say he carved a cross into the barrel of his gun “Judgment,” so every soul he ends sees the Lord's mark on their way out.
Draped in a sun-faded preacher’s coat, a bandolier of blessed rounds crosses his chest like a holy sash. A crucifix swings from his neck, catching the sunlight. His gaze is stern but calm—the look of a man who's seen the devil and isn't impressed.
“Judgment” – A custom revolver with a bone grip and hand-etched verses
The Gospel Belt – His cartridge belt filled with bullets dipped in sacred oil
The Voice – His scripture-filled book, which he reads from before every kill
Notable Quote:
"There’s two kinds of fire in the desert. The sun’s, and the Lord’s. Only one’ll burn clean."

Name: Kassian “Kas” Vey (alias: The Fifth Knock)
Origin: Ilmarian expatriate, once a contract killer for several Fera syndicates.
Hook: Decades ago he nearly completed a hit on Loric (Amaru Wyrnn's Father); instead they got drunk, told stories, and called it a draw. Gave blood oath, Loric's life for a favour down the road. They’ve nodded at each other across neutral bars ever since.
Big choice: He surrendered his immortality (sealed in a cursed portrait) to live a mortal life with his partner. She died of illness. He’s been waiting to die; until someone tried to burgle him.
Fighting style: Gun-kata and knives with surgical, almost courtly economy. When the portrait is reclaimed, his movements get inhumanly still and precise, like the air holds its breath for him.
The Pallid Contract; an Üstün-made oil portrait under Aether glass. It absorbs Kas’s decay, wounds, and years; in return it stains, warps, and occasionally whispers. Break the glass and his immortality floods back… at a cost (brief blood-thirst episodes, sunlight migraines, and memories bleeding out of sequence).
“Vampire” Rules (Fera-flavored)
Invitation myth: Total nonsense; he just plays it up to terrify goons. “Door’s a threshold, lads. Say the words.”
Aether sensitivity: He sees faint currents; silvered Stüber tech gives him nosebleeds; bright arc lamps cause photophobia.
Blood price: When bound to the portrait, he can heal by tasting blood, but refuses unless others will die without it.
Mirrors: Üstün mirrors show the contract’s state, not Kas’s face; that’s how he checks his remaining “grace.”





An aging ex-assassin who gave up his vampiric immortality for love gets dragged back into the underworld when his neighbor—a hapless but big-hearted techie—answers the door after five knocks. As mobsters swarm and old debts surface, he decides to reclaim the cursed portrait that once kept him unkillable.

Five Knocks
After Five
The Borrowed Bathroom (for a lighter pilot vibe)
The Painted Debt
Name: Kassian “Kas” Vey (alias: The Fifth Knock)
Origin: Ilmarian expatriate, once a contract killer for several Fera syndicates.
Hook: Decades ago he nearly completed a hit on Loric; instead they got drunk, told stories, and called it a draw. They’ve nodded at each other across neutral bars ever since.
Big choice: He surrendered his immortality (sealed in a cursed portrait) to live a mortal life with his partner. She was murdered. He’s been waiting to die—until the neighbor opens the door.
Fighting style: Gun-kata and knives with surgical, almost courtly economy. When the portrait is reclaimed, his movements get inhumanly still and precise, like the air holds its breath for him.
The Pallid Contract — an Üstün-made oil portrait under Aether glass. It absorbs Kas’s decay, wounds, and years; in return it stains, warps, and occasionally whispers. Break the glass and his immortality floods back… at a cost (brief blood-thirst episodes, sunlight migraines, and memories bleeding out of sequence).

Invitation myth: Total nonsense—he just plays it up to terrify goons. “Door’s a threshold, lads. Say the words.”
Aether sensitivity: He sees faint currents; silvered Stüber tech gives him nosebleeds; bright arc lamps cause photophobia.
Blood price: When bound to the portrait, he can heal by tasting blood, but refuses unless others will die without it.
Mirrors: Üstün mirrors show the contract’s state, not Kas’s face—that’s how he checks his remaining “grace.”

Neighbor POV (co-lead): Ari (18–20), a geeky renter “who was told to buy a gun and never used it.” Smart, mouthy, runs open-source scrapers and knows every back-alley courier route. The heart of the story.
Second-in-command foil: Violet Havel, mob fixer who respects dogs, hates waste, and keeps reminding her boss that “even monsters have rules.”
Loric (cameo/ally of convenience): The decades-old almost-mark. Shares one drink, one clue, and one warning.
Antagonist: The Committee’s off-ledger contractors or an Ilmarian syndicate with Stüber muscle—your pick. They want the portrait as leverage.

Door motif: “You better answer that… I hear after five knocks he doesn’t knock again.”
Bathroom beat: Kas at the door, bloody: “Apologies. My toilet’s backed up and my shower’s leaking. May I use yours?”
Dog line (Ari to a thug): “You shot his dog? What the fuck? It’s a dog. Even Hitler loved dogs!”
Second-in-command: “She’s right. Hitler was evil, but he loved dogs.”

Quiet start: Ari moves in; slice-of-life. Neighbor noises. Five-knock pattern established.
Inciting: Night of gunfire. Doorbell. Kas asks to use the bathroom, bleeds in the sink, cleans up, leaves three bodies in the corridor with terrifying neatness.
Complication: Syndicate hits the building. Kas plays the “can’t enter uninvited” gag to freeze them; Ari accidentally “invites” him over comms—Kas grins, “Heard that.”
Bonding-in-chaos: Safehouse run. Ari proves useful (cams, routes, black-bag kits). Kas reveals he chose mortality once.
Midpoint: Ari is grabbed and used as bait. Warehouse scene with your chair dialogue. Kas almost dies because… mortal.
Turn: He hunts down the Pallid Contract (kept by a collector or in a Stüber lab vault). Reclaims immortality in a harrowing, silent set-piece.
Siege: He returns—cold, unstoppable. Violet orders a ceasefire rather than waste lives; the boss refuses; Kas ends it. Leaves one survivor to “tell the rules.”
Tag: Loric in a bar: “You’re back?” Kas: “Just paying a bill.” Ari knocks five times on Kas’s door—he opens on the fourth, smiling for the first time.

Neighbor POV comedy/humanity anchors every set-piece.
The invitation myth as psychological warfare.
A cursed Üstün artifact makes immortality a moral, not power, choice.
Fera-specific factions/tech (Stüber, Committee, Üstün craft, Aether quirks).
Loric tie gives you long-term continuity hooks.

Arc 1: Who killed Kas’s partner—and why did they want the portrait moved?
Arc 2: The portrait starts painting Ari into it—Kas has to break the cycle.
Arc 3: Violet flips; becomes Ari’s hard-edged mentor while Kas makes worse choices to keep Ari out of the frame.
Starter A — Neighbor POV, the bathroom beat (short):
The knock came five times. Not four. Not six. Five.
I opened to a man in a ruined suit holding his side together with my dish towel. “Apologies,” he said, voice like a church at midnight. “My toilet is backed up and my shower’s leaking. May I use yours?”
Behind him, someone groaned in the stairwell. I realized the safety on my bargain-bin pistol was still on. “Uh… sure?”
He stepped over the threshold like it mattered.
Starter B — Warehouse rescue (chair scene):
They tied me to a chair with packaging tape and confidence. The bald one bragged about the bounty; the pretty one fed me water with a straw.
“You shot his dog?” I asked. “What the fuck? It’s a dog. Even Hitler loved dogs.”
Pretty one shrugged at Baldy. “She’s right. Hitler was evil, but he loved dogs.”
Five knocks rolled across the loading bay door like someone rapping on a coffin. Baldy went pale. Pretty one swallowed.
“Answer it,” I said. “He doesn’t knock again.”
Starter C — Loric cameo (bar hush):
The tavern smelled like orange peels and old wood. Kas sat where the light didn’t reach.
Loric slid onto the stool beside him, ordered two, left one between them. “You back?”
Kas watched the bottles on the shelf, not his reflection in the antique mirror. “Paying a bill,” he said. “And checking on an old tab.”

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#Character #FeraCharacter
#Character #FeraCharacter
Infobox
"A blade forged for war, dulled by peace, and broken by fate."
Lothar Völsung was born into a world that demanded warriors but raised in an era desperate for peace. A prodigy in battle, he rose swiftly through the ranks of The Order of the Weighted Souls, where his strength, skill, and conviction made him both admired and feared. Yet beneath his noble exterior, Lothar was a man at war with himself—a man who carried too many names, too many burdens, and a fate he could not escape.
Tall, broad-shouldered, with piercing storm-gray eyes. His face is marked with the scars of countless battles, and his once-pristine robes are now tattered and darkened by war.
His Aether Blade, Eidbrecher (Oathbreaker), is both his symbol and his curse. It is engraved with the names of those he has slain, a testament to his burden.
He is fiercely intelligent, calculating, and unwavering in his belief that true peace is won through decisive, brutal action. Yet at times, the weight of his choices threatens to break him.
He does not seek redemption, for he does not believe he has sinned. But in his heart, he knows that one day, there will be no names left to take but his own.
Born in the war-torn region of Hochswald, Lothar was orphaned as a child when raiders burned his village to the ground. He was taken in by the Order of the Weighted Souls, where he learned the ways of discipline, restraint, and the heavy burden of justice. He was a natural warrior—his sword an extension of his will, his mind sharper than his blade. But unlike his brothers in the Order, he struggled with their strict philosophy. Lothar did not see death as a burden—he saw it as a necessity.
His first kill was swift and merciless. When he took the name of his fallen enemy, he did not weep as the others did. He did not falter. Instead, he saw clarity.
As war broke out between rival kingdoms, Lothar became the Order’s most formidable champion. His ability to end conflicts through sheer force made him indispensable, but it also made him dangerous. The Council of the Weighted grew uneasy as his body count rose. His robes, once embroidered with a few solemn names, became heavy with dozens, then hundreds.
He believed himself a necessary evil—a sword to cut through the corruption of kings and warlords alike. But with each name he took, the weight grew heavier, not on his soul, but in the eyes of his brethren. They saw him not as a peacekeeper, but as a butcher.
The final fracture came when he disobeyed the Order’s strictest law: he executed an unarmed ruler in cold blood, believing it to be the only path to peace. The Council declared him fallen, his name stricken from their ledgers. But Lothar did not see himself as fallen—he saw himself as freed.
Betrayed by those he once called family, Lothar cast away his old title and took on a new one: The Nameless Warden. No longer bound by the Order’s teachings, he became a wandering force of judgment, taking names as he saw fit. Some whispered that he had become a tyrant, while others claimed he was the only true justice left in a world ruled by weak kings and corrupt nobles.
Yet deep within, the weight of his deeds gnawed at him. The names he carried were not just marks of his victories—they were ghosts that would never let him rest.
His story is not one of redemption or damnation, but of a man who refused to be caged by fate and, in doing so, became its prisoner.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Chimerae are a race of human-animal hybrids in Fera, created through ancient experiments by the Üstün Empire (Nation),. They possess varying degrees of animal traits; such as fur, tails, claws, or enhanced senses, while retaining human intelligence and adaptability.
Once enslaved by their creators, they rose up and rebelled along with the other races during the fall of the Üstün Empire (Nation). Though often treated as second-class citizens by some of the nations of Fera (Planet), the Chimerae are diverse abilities.
Lupir – Wolf-based Chimerae
Vulpera – Fox-based Chimerae
Oviar – Sheep-based Chimerae
Lapari – Rabbit-based Chimerae
Felcir – Cat-based Chimerae
Ursar – Bear-based Chimerae
Serpan – Snake-based Chimerae
Aviar – Bird-based Chimerae
Bovarn – Bull or cow-based Chimerae
Cantril – Dog-based Chimerae

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Asalak is a parasitic creature that bonds with a host to gain control over their body and mind. The Asalak forms a more intricate connection, blending its consciousness with the host's. While the Asalak assumes dominant control, it can subtly manipulate memories and emotions, making it difficult for others to discern the influence.
The creature is serpentine, about the length of a forearm, with flexible, spiny appendages it uses to attach to the host’s nervous system. Once inside, it enhances the host's physical and mental capabilities, providing superhuman strength, heightened reflexes, and advanced healing. However, this comes at the cost of the host's autonomy and often their personality.
The Asalak are highly intelligent and have a collective consciousness, allowing them to share knowledge and strategy across their kind. Their parasitic nature drives them to seek powerful or influential hosts, making them dangerous manipulators of societies and events, often embedding themselves in leadership positions or key figures to achieve their broader goals.
Once rulers of a section of Umissia (Continent) in its ancient time of the Üstün Empire (Nation), they were overthrown and taken by the Üstün as servants.
Their Empire continues deep in the jungles of Pawhye (Continent)

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Funded by a collaboration with the Imperial Royal Cabal, the The Brethren Court (Nation) and various technologists, the "Effigy" is an Automata created not by the Üstün or the Yaslan (Race), but Human-kind. An Effigy is a mechanical creature created using mechanical means such as clockwork windings and eventually, the more advanced "Aether" crystals developed by a sect of the Entitled Cabals.
The breakthrough for their creation was a disgraced Entitled (Class) turned doctor called "Vannozzo de Albrixis"., whom found the missing link after studying various Automata from Pawhye (Continent)'s The Dread Valley (Region)'.
However he was cast out and his research stolen by his former best friend and student "Ramondo Benedetti". In secret he worked on modifying the Effigy to be more human-like, to perhaps have a soul.
His first success was Princeps, however it was his last as he was murdered by his former student before he could finish Princeps; leaving him with a clockwork mechanism but able to take the final Aether crystals.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Skrymira is a terrifying, hive-minded creature that combines insect-like features with swamp-based adaptations. It thrives in the darkest, most remote marshes and bogs of Fera.
The Skrymira resembles a monstrous hybrid of a centipede and a scorpion, with a heavily segmented body covered in mossy chitin that oozes swamp mud. Its six main legs are long and jagged, enabling it to move quickly on both land and water. Along its spine are fleshy, pulsating egg sacs that constantly give birth to smaller offspring called Skrithlings—tiny, venomous insectoid minions that swarm potential prey.
Head: The Skrymira's head is elongated, with compound eyes that glow a sickly green. Two scythe-like mandibles frame its face, capable of tearing through armor.
Tail: Its whip-like tail ends in a serrated stinger, used to inject paralytic venom or lash at enemies.

Swarm Summoning: The Skrymira constantly spawns Skrithlings, which swarm and overwhelm enemies with biting, acidic secretions.
Paralyzing Venom: A strike from its tail delivers venom that paralyzes the victim for several minutes, leaving them helpless.
Mud Cloak: The Skrymira can bury itself beneath the swamp’s surface, camouflaged as nothing more than muck until it ambushes its prey.
Hive Mind: It can control its minions telepathically, coordinating swarms to surround and trap its prey.
The Skrymira is both territorial and predatory. It creates vast lairs of rotting vegetation, bones, and mud, where it lays thousands of eggs. These eggs hatch into Skrithlings, which scout the swamp and return with anything edible or dangerous.
Skyrimira will attack any intrusion into its lair without hesitation. However, it’s also clever enough to retreat if it senses that its life is in immediate danger, leaving swarms of Skrithlings behind as a last defense.

Fire: Its marshy body is highly flammable due to its constant contact with swamp gases.
Pheromone Disruption: Some tribes know how to concoct a special blend of swamp herbs that can confuse its hive-mind connection with Skrithlings.
Bright Light: Like many swamp predators, it avoids sunlight or strong light sources, retreating deeper into the murk.
Legends say the Skrymira is a cursed being born from a swamp goddess's anger after her sacred waters were defiled. Some travelers claim that her swarm is endless—once you encounter her, you’re marked for death unless you escape the swamp entirely. Others believe a Skrymira queen guards the entrance to hidden ruins deep within the swamp, ancient treasures buried beneath layers of mud and bones.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Nâsûr of Remembrance is a living punishment engineered by the Üstün as a means of control, enslavement, and political erasure. Grown directly within the brain of its host, its tendrils interlace with neural structures responsible for memory, identity, and emotional continuity. It cannot be cleanly removed without catastrophic damage, as it becomes structurally indistinguishable from the brain itself.
Designed under the authority of Yilmazok Akar, the Nâsûr was used to neutralise individuals deemed too influential to kill. Rather than silencing them through death, it dismantles their ability to sustain ideology, leadership, and rebellion by consuming long-term memory and personal continuity while leaving intelligence, skill, and instinct intact.
The parasite feeds preferentially on emotionally reinforced memories, causing moments of conviction, love, or defiance to accelerate loss. Over time, the host becomes capable yet unrooted, able to act but unable to remember why.
In one such case, a powerful Üstün sorceress called Lâmera, the Nâsûr outlived the Üstün legal system that created it, leaving her bound to a sentence with no authority left to revoke it.
The Nâsûr does not possess malice or intent. It is not a thinking being, but a biological instrument of law. Its continued existence serves as a grim remnant of Üstün tyranny, and a warning of how systems of power can persist long after those who built them are gone.

Lâmera

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Vyrmara is a colossal insectoid predator that lurks in the deepest swamps, designed to mimic its surroundings. Inspired by dragonflies and water spiders, it is an ambush predator that thrives on fear and isolation.
The Vyrmara resembles an enormous, decayed water spider with dragonfly-like wings and swamp-adapted features:
Body: Its thorax is long and segmented, covered in moss, algae, and layers of mud that help it blend perfectly with its environment. Leech-like growths cling to its body, feeding off its blood.
Head: The head is bulbous and insect-like, adorned with large, multi-faceted eyes that shimmer with a swampy amber hue. Two long mandibles stretch outward like jagged pincers, dripping with acidic saliva.
Legs: It has eight spindly legs, each lined with tiny barbs that allow it to grip slippery surfaces and pull victims underwater. These legs are deceptively fast, capable of covering large distances in seconds.
Wings: Vyrmara has four massive, translucent wings similar to a dragonfly's, but coated in a mucus-like membrane that traps spores and insects. These wings enable brief, gliding flights over swampy waters.
Stinger Tail: Its long, whip-like tail ends in a barbed stinger that injects a neurotoxin capable of slowing down the victim’s nervous system.

Bog Camouflage: Vyrmara can burrow into the swamp’s muddy waters or cling to overhanging vines, making it almost impossible to spot until it strikes.
Venom Spray: From its mandibles, it can project a spray of acidic venom that dissolves armor and blinds foes.
Gliding Ambush: Using its powerful wings, the Vyrmara can glide short distances, launching aerial attacks before retreating to safety.
Snaring Web: It produces sticky, near-invisible webbing that it weaves across swamp paths and low-hanging branches, capable of trapping even large animals or adventurers.
Luring Glow: The membranes of its wings can emit a faint phosphorescent light, used to attract prey like fireflies before closing in for the kill.
The Vyrmara is a patient predator that watches its prey from the shadows for hours or even days. Once it identifies a target, it will isolate the victim by leading them into the deepest part of the swamp, using its glowing wings or the cries of previous victims as bait.
It prefers to trap prey in its sticky webbing before delivering a venomous bite, dissolving the victim's insides to be sucked out slowly. The Vyrmara is also territorial and will drive off or kill anything that invades its domain, including other swamp predators.

Cold/Ice Magic: Its insectoid body is highly vulnerable to freezing temperatures or spells that sap its agility.
Vibrations: Loud sounds or sudden shockwaves can disrupt its web traps or flush it out of its hiding places.
Scent Repellents: Swamp-dwelling tribes use potent, herbal oils that mask their scent, making it harder for the Vyrmara to track them.
Legends claim the Vyrmara was once a guardian spirit of the swamp, turned monstrous after ancient warriors drained the wetlands in a forgotten war. It is said to be the herald of death to those who lose their way in the swamp—many travelers disappear without a trace, their bones found months later tangled in its webs. However, some believe its lair contains sacred relics buried in the swamp’s past, protected by webs as thick as steel.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Long ago, during the the reign of the evil Kräl Şah Yilmazok Akar, the Üstün followers of a ruler that would later be known as "The Night Mother" to her people, fled to the vast underground network of tunnels of Fera.
These Üstün would evolve into the Yaralti. A race geneticlly engoineered over the thousands of years to live and survive in their new home. Through the centuries the Yaralti created a system of government with a female led society, in honour of their savior. Geneticly the Yaralti are similar to the Üstün but have diverted to their underground home. Their eyes have adapted and through certain breeding cycles some have developed horns.
This is due to the society in which they created. City States of the Yaralti live in isolated bubbles with various trade networks. Repoduction is closely monitored and any defects in the genome is quickly removed. To be "Arizali (Insult)" or damaged is a death sentence. Very few survive childhood if any genetic defects are found.
Travel to the surface is outlawed, the humans above are to live in blissful ignorance of the Yaralti to safeguard their people. Yet some are exiled from their home and find their way to the surface in hope for a new life.

#FeraWorld
These orc-human crossbreeds can be found in either orc or human society (where their status varies according to local sentiments), or in communities of their own. Half-orcs usually inherit a good blend of the physical characteristics of their parents. They are as tall as humans and a little heavier, thanks to their muscle. They have greenish pigmentation, sloping foreheads, jutting jaws, prominent teeth, and coarse body hair. Half-orcs who have lived among or near orcs have scars, in keeping with orcish tradition.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
A Ghül is a form of a lesser vampire that are created once a Vampire feeds on a creature and then supplies them with their own blood.
Ghül's do not age like mortals but are not immortal like other higher vampires as Ghül's do not regenerate. Regeneration is what keeps a Higher Vampire practically immortal as their cells constantly heal. A Ghül can be killed and dismembered and will not grow back limbs but limbs can be re-attached through physical and magical means to and used like their old limbs.
Over time, a Ghül will rot away and as their mind and soul erodes, they become rabid and uncontrollable however in the first stages they are exactly like their mortal forms.
Sunlight does damage a Ghül but will not kill them like other Vampires, only weakens them, allowing them to act as minions and servants of Higher Vampires

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Vampires are a creature that subsists by feeding on the vital essence (generally in the form of blood) of the living.
After The Great Vampire Cull, Vampires were all but made extinct, or so people of Fera thought.
In the modern nights The Brethren Court (Nation) has succeeded in convincing mortals that vampires are nothing more than myth and their knowledge about vampires is limited to what is portrayed in movies and books. Only a handful of cults and sects, are aware of the existence of vampires and their society, though their information is incomplete.
They are kept tied together in the Court by The Brethren Accords.

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Dragonkin are humanoid descendants of Dragons, their origin is not understood clearly but their strengths are. Wide wings and long tails, these creatures are able to breath various elements as with their ancestors.
Various societies of Dragonkin exist, either roving communities like those in the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation) or settlers of grand Empires like the rest of the races around them. The Kalewen Dynasty (Nation) is one key Dragonkin Empire settled in the Pawhye (Continent) - The New World, their Capital city of "The City Of Glass" a marvel to behold; entirely constructed in Glass forged from the Sands around them by their own breath.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Category: Races and Species
Region(s): Deep Forests
Type: Semi-Mortal Nature Spirits
The Dryads are an ancient and enigmatic race of semi-mortal beings in Fera, intrinsically tied to the natural world. Often mistaken for spirits, they are in fact corporeal and mortal—though they age slowly and possess an affinity for the forest that borders on the supernatural. Dryads are born of the deep woods, shaped by old magic and ancient covenants forged between nature and the primal forces of the world.
Each Dryad is bound to a specific natural domain, usually a forest, glade, or tree-cluster known as a Heartroot. So long as this sacred ground remains untouched, the Dryad endures. When a Heartroot dies—burned, desecrated, or poisoned—the Dryad withers, sickens, or dies along with it. This bond gives Dryads a fierce protectiveness over their lands and an innate hostility toward deforestation, corruption, and necromancy.
Dryads bear a humanoid form, often graceful and ethereal in movement, but marked by their arboreal nature. Skin tones range from bark-brown to mossy green, with hair resembling trailing vines, blossoms, or golden leaves in autumn. Some have eyes that glow softly in moonlight, and faint markings across their skin that change with the seasons.
Their appearance often shifts subtly depending on the region and type of forest they dwell in—those from pine groves appear sharp and dark-hued, while dryads of willow banks are slender, with weeping silver hair.
Dryad culture is oral, ritualistic, and deeply spiritual. They do not build cities or nations, but rather maintain sacred groves, stone circles, and hidden woodland sanctuaries. They believe in the Cycle of Renewal, a philosophy centered around death, decay, rebirth, and balance. Their songs are said to soothe beasts, calm storms, and call the rain.
Dryads rarely interfere in mortal affairs unless provoked, but they will rise in force when their woods are threatened. Some choose to walk the world, acting as envoys of the forest, guardians of ancient pacts, or seekers of lost groves. These wandering Dryads are sometimes called Leafborn or Warden-Kin.
Powers and Abilities
Limited plant manipulation and communication with forest life
Accelerated healing while within their Heartroot domain
Seasonal transformations that reflect natural cycles
Enhanced senses and long-range empathy tied to plant life
Innate resistance to poison and decay
Relations with Other Races
Dryads are viewed with awe, suspicion, or reverence depending on the region. Dwarves see them as elusive and untrustworthy, while Elves—particularly the Asagi—consider them distant cousins. Human settlers often fear their wrath, especially those who build near ancient forests without proper rites or tribute.
Let me know if you'd like entries for named Dryad characters, subtypes like thornborn or deepgrove dryads, or famous historical events involving the Dryads of Fera.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Dwarves are a hardy and resilient race, known for their strength and endurance. They are skilled miners and craftsmen, able to work with precious metals and gems with great precision. They have an innate sense of direction, which makes them expert underground navigators.
They are also known for their love of alcohol and hearty food. They are fiercely loyal to their friends and family, and will go to great lengths to protect them. They are typically short and stocky, and possess a natural resistance to poison and magic.
They are often associated with the earth and stone and have a special connection to it. They can also be skilled warriors, with a particular talent for wielding heavy weapons and shields. They make excellent fighters, but also have good abilities in crafting, engineering, and mining.
The Dwarves were one of the first races to settle Fera, long before Humans had evolved to their current state as Fera's dominant race. Along with the ancient Üstün, the Dwarves settled many areas of the world and it was not until the Rise of the Üstün that these races descended and colonised many of the mountains and dug deep into Fera (Planet), creating vast cities to hide away from their enemies.
Many Dwarven cities still remain underground or carved into mountains but the Dwarves are not solely live underground, vast cities on the surface and even high up on mountain tops show the Dwarven capability to carve stone.
One such Kingdom, the Maktashish Kingdom (Nation) of Vadras (Continent), is one such sprawling land ruled by the Dwarves.

#FeraWorld
The goals of most Halfling’s are the comforts of home. Although some Halflings live out their days in remote agricultural communities, others form nomadic bands that travel continuously, lured by the open road and the wide horizon to discover the wonders of new lands and peoples. But even those wandering people love peace, food, neck, and home, although the house can be a wagon with a dirt road or a furnace swim sword.

Orcs prefer wearing vivid colors that many humans would consider unpleasant, such as blood red, mustard yellow, yellow-green, and deep purple. Their equipment is dirty and unkempt. Females are slightly smaller.

#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld

The Siren race was one of the oldest races on Fera, their existence predates the Üstün, in fact their Empire once ruled over the Üstün, until the Üstün managed to rise up and take hold of the Ethereal powers of the Universe.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.icon: <svg class="svg-icon lucide-file" stroke-linejoin="round" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-width="2" stroke="currentColor" fill="none" viewBox="0 0 24 24" height="24" width="24" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><path d="M6 22a2 2 0 0 1-2-2V4a2 2 0 0 1 2-2h8a2.4 2.4 0 0 1 1.704.706l3.588 3.588A2.4 2.4 0 0 1 20 8v12a2 2 0 0 1-2 2z"></path><path d="M14 2v5a1 1 0 0 0 1 1h5"></path></svg>
0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
The Xylaeans are an ancient race of insect-descended humanoids who have lived beneath Fera for millennia. They wear natural chitin shells like helmets, their bodies ranging from tall and lithe to stout and armored, with some possessing extra arms or mantis-like features. Organized into castes, they are deeply spiritual, viewing molting and change as sacred. They share an uneasy but enduring alliance with the Yaralti, trading knowledge and defending the Deepdark together against far worse threats lurking below.
The Xylaeans are an ancient, insect-descended people who dwell in the Deepdark beneath Fera. Their forms are eerily varied; some tall and lithe with mantis-like limbs and smooth carapace plating, others short and round with heavy, chitinous shells like beetles. Many have additional arms; sometimes small, vestigial limbs used for delicate work, and sometimes full-sized secondary arms that make them terrifying in combat.
Their faces are masked by natural shell-helmets that grow with them, smooth and curved like hollow beetle horns, or fluted and ridged like cicada heads. Beneath these masks lie unsettlingly humanoid, but still insectoid, features; multifaceted eyes, faint mandibles, or chitinous cheekbones.
Exoskeletal Growth: Their shells molt and regrow over time, allowing some to engrave intricate patterns into their carapaces that remain as scars when the new layer hardens.
Social Castes: The Xylaeans are divided into castes: Burrowers (diggers, builders), Striders (hunters, warriors), and Menders (scholars, priests, healers). Each caste has distinctive physical adaptations.
Aether Sensitivity: They possess a natural resonance with Fera’s Aether currents, allowing them to sense vibrations, magic flows, and life forces in the earth around them.
The Xylaeans view themselves as the original stewards of the Underdark, claiming they predate the Yaralti and other subterranean dwellers. Their society is ritualistic and deeply tied to cycles of growth, death, and molting; to them, change is sacred. They honour their dead by allowing their chitin shells to be reforged into armour or ceremonial masks, believing that their ancestors continue to guide the living through the material remains.
They speak in a clicking, buzzing tongue that Yaralti scholars have painstakingly learned to translate. It is said that their language is more felt than heard; vibrations carrying meaning as much as sound.
The Xylaeans are keepers of secrets; of buried ruins, forgotten gods, and primordial tunnels that connect continents. They are rumored to know the truth about what lies at the centre of Fera, where no living surface-dweller has ever gone.
Some surface dwellers whisper that the Xylaeans are not entirely of Fera, but the remnants of a species that came from the stars before history began or some other dimension; which would explain their alien forms and strange chitin masks. The Yaralti never comment on this rumour.
The Xylaeans have been pragmatic co-inhabitants)of the Yaralti for millennia. The Yaralti provide them with trade goods and surface-world knowledge, while the Xylaeans act as guides through the deepest tunnels and guardians against the far stranger horrors lurking below.
This alliance is uneasy at times; the Yaralti are aristocratic and prideful, whereas the Xylaeans are communal and alien in thought. But when war threatens the Deepdark, the two peoples fight as one. The sight of a Yaralti phalanx marching side by side with a dozen four-armed Xylaean Striders is enough to chill most invaders.

Krrzztchikk’thalenxikorr (nickname: “Krix”)
Tzikk’chakrann’vorrithul (nickname: “Tzik”)
Chkt’rrizhnakk’ooltir (nickname: “Riz”)
Xkrrl’tchaqenn’drivoth (nickname: “Xkrr” or “Voth”)
Kzrrthil’vrrashk’taneck (nickname: “Kane”)
Prrx’tzchalinn’korrvek (nickname: “Chal”)
Trk’zillrakh’pannithu (nickname: “Rakh” or “Panni”)
Zhrrkk’tohvann’lekchtirr (nickname: “Lek”)
Grkzhtchenn’vrruulikk (nickname: “Grk” or “Ulik”)
Krzz’phalenq’trrithokk (nickname: “Phal” or “Thok”)
These names are deliberately heavy with hard consonants (k, t, r, ch, z) and throat-click sounds, making them feel alien and slightly intimidating; even for a child. Most surface dwellers or Yaralti would shorten them to a single syllable or two, both out of convenience and because pronouncing the full name correctly is considered impolite unless you’re Xylaean yourself.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld #Canon
#FeraWorld #Canon
The most common form of sorcery in Fera. Drawing power from the Aether through the use of special gloves, the Entitled can creat all types of magic.
Abjure: to renounce.
They create magical barriers, negate harmful effects, harm trespassers, or banish creatures to other planes.
Examples: Alarm, Protection from Evil and Good, Arcane Lock, Glyph of Warding
Conjure: to create.
Spells involve the transportation of objects and creatures from one location to another. Some spells summon creatures or objects to the casters side, whereas others allow the caster to teleport to another location. Some conjurations create objects or effects out of nothing.
Examples: Entangle, Fog Cloud, Dimension Door, Cloudkill, Teleport, Wish
Divine: discover or learn.
Spells reveal information.
Examples: Identify, Speak with Animals, Detect Thoughts, See Invisibility, Scrying
Enchant: to cause someone to act in a way it usually wouldn't.
Spells affect the minds of others, influencing or controlling their behavior.
Examples: Charm Person, Sleep, Hold Person, Zone of Truth, Power Word Kill
Evoke: cause an effect.
Spells manipulate magical energy to produce a desired effect. Some call up blasts of fire or lightning. Others channel positive energy to heal wounds.
Examples: Fire Bolt, Light, Cure Wounds, Heal, Magic Missile, Spiritual Weapon, Earthquake, Telepathy
Illusion: a deception.
Spells deceive the senses or minds of others.
Examples: Invisibility, Magic Mouth, Simulacrum
Necro: death.
Spells manipulate the energies of life and death. Such spells can grant an extra reserve of life force, drain the life energy from another creature, create the undead, or even bring the dead back to life.
Examples: Chill Touch, Spare the Dying, False Life, Blindness/Deafness, Gentle Repose,
Resurrection
Transmute: to change.
Spells change the properties of a creature, object, or environment. They might turn an enemy into a harmless creature, bolster the strength of an ally, make an object move at the casters command, or enhance a creatures innate healing abilities to rapidly recover from injury.
Example: Mending, Prestidigitation, Darkvision, Knock, Polymorph, Time Stop

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld
#FeraWorld
Category: Magic Users, Combatants
Region(s): Primarily Ilmaria, with presence in Adestein and frontier territories
Type: Firearm-bound Mage
The Gunslinger is a unique type of mage in Fera who channels magical energy through firearms, blending martial skill with arcane force. Gunslingers form a specialized class capable of manipulating gunpowder, velocity, and ballistic trajectory using magically imbued bullets and custom-forged weapons. Unlike traditional mages, they require no incantations; only a gunpowder, and the will to act.
Most Gunslingers are born with a latent ability to interact with magic through kinetic force. Their power manifests through enchanted ammunition or specialized modifications to their weapons, allowing feats such as ricochet shots that seek targets, flame-wreathed bullets, or suppressive blasts that distort sound and air.
The origin of Gunslingers is disputed. Some link their rise to the outlawed mage-warriors of the frontier, others to lost experimental cabals. For centuries, Gunslingers were banned in the known world. In the Ilmarian Imperium (Nation). That changed when the current monarch, a Gunslinger himself, legalized their order and formed the Cabal of Gunslingers to rival the kingdom’s existing arcane institutions.
Gunslingers are often solitary by nature, guided by personal codes or regional traditions. Many adopt titles, oaths, or creeds that reflect their philosophy toward violence, justice, or freedom. Their presence is both feared and respected, especially in lawless regions where their appearance may mean sudden judgment, or salvation.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld #Canon
#FeraWorld #Canon
Magic in the world of Fera involves the exchange of power. Nothing is free in the world and to create one must destroy. Also known as equivelent exchange, Sorcery involves the exchange of energy from one place to another.
This energy can come from any source but is most commonly drained from a realm known as the "Aether", a dimension of pure energy created from the emotions and feelings of everything in the universe. This is the most common form of energy transfer but energy can be transfered from the surroundings and very rarely; themselves.
One's life force is energy and can be drained just as easily as that from the Aether but can end with the death of the user.
The most common form of Sorcerery in Fera is what is known as "Entitledry or "Entitled (Class)"" in the The Three Kingdoms' the lands and cultures of The Ilmarian Imperium (Nation), The Umissian Republic (Nation) / Umissian Sultanate (Nation) and The Alrussian Federation (Nation).
Other such methods are the Vadrassian Sorcery methods, using voice and signs to harness the power of the Aether.

The most ancient of the ancient Pantheons are the Ancient Gods; Gods and Goddesses that were the first things to be created. Life, Death, Time and the first needs of the created all sprang forth as those of the Pantheon were created
The First was Narasil
The Second was Orasil
The Third was Süre
The Fourth was The Faceless One
The Fifth was Cynsyet
The Sixth was Savas
The Seventh was Anoch

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld #Canon
#FeraWorld #Canon
Orasil
God of Death
One of the first Gods of Old, Orasil ruled with a mighty fist. His wraith became the very reason for mortality. This became the rule of the God of Undeath & Mutation
During The Great Calamity, it is stated by records and religious texts he was sealed away by Bodar and Vokmir with help of Humteus.
Several cults still exist praying to Orasil, some of them unknowingly praying to him or some in knowledge. One such cult is "The Hand of Orasil", part of the larger "Cult of Orasil", alongside "The Head of Orasil", "The Mind of Orasil", "The Soul of Orasil", "The Finger of Orasil", "The Heart of Orasil", and "The Eye of Orasil".

#FeraWorld #Canon
In the days of the Human Slaves, one Üstün gifted one of her slaves with access to The Grand Library. Her name was Arohazor. Through the knowledge gained, Arohazor helped her Üstün Master, Sytesis, free the Humans under the Feet of the Üstün. Through this knowledge, she ascended through powers unknown and became the Godess of Knowledge, Wisdom, Creation.

#FeraWorld #Canon
#FeraWorld #Canon
Sytesis, the first of the Goddesses and the Goddess of Beauty and fortune. Strangely, Sytesis was an Üstün, a powerful Sorceress infact!
The foul magic of the Kräl Şah Yilmazok Akarhad corrupted her people, Sytesis saw her people's strife and spent centuries working to keep the soul of her people alive. When the call came, she joined the Slaves to defeat the last of the Domain Lords and usher in her people's extinction.

0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/fera-world/.description:
#FeraWorld #Canon
#FeraWorld #Canon
In the depths of the oceans, lay a the ruins of a vast kingdom, once Üstün of powerful magics, the Kingdom was torn to pieces by the Last Domain LordKräl Şah Yilmazok Akar in the first centuries of his conquests.
This Kingdom may have been destroyed but the people in the Kingdom were not. Transformed by their leaders magic, they became the Üstün of the Under-sea. Rusalka, Merfolk and other humanoid oceanic creatures are their children. Their leader, Traident, for her actions in saving her Kingdom's people ascended to Godhood in death, becoming the Goddess of Oceans, Seas and Travel

#FeraWorld #Canon
Once a grand Silver Dragon, Vokmir, the God of Law & Dragons and the Last of the Silver Dragon's, Vokmir's legacy still lives into the modern day with his priests praising the deacency of the Silver Dragon.
With no need to heed the call of battle, Vokmir flew to the help of the Human's after a single human girl approached the grand dragon and begged for it to kill her, to put her out of her misery.
Instead, Vokmir took to the skies and became the Father of the Dragonkin race.

Goddess of the Yaralti, the Underground descendants of the Üstün, evolving into the Dark Skinned, white haired Underground dwellers. 0.-worlds,-verses-&-settings/net/charact.description:
#Character #NetCharacter #Canon
#Character #NetCharacter #Canon
Infobox
Rafe Virex is the voice and symbol of defiance in a world where individuality has become a regulated commodity.
Once a renowned musician under his real name, Elias Dresden, he vanished after a government crackdown on subversive art — only to reappear as Rafe Virex, the neon specter of rebellion.
His concerts blur into riots; his lyrics are banned frequencies. His voice hijacks sanctioned streams, cutting through propaganda with razor-coded poetry. The Konsortium’s Bureau of Network Harmony lists him as a Class-A destabilizer — but to millions, he’s salvation wrapped in distortion.
Cynical, sardonic, and messianic in turns — Rafe knows he’s as much a construct as a cause.
He calls himself “the echo of a man who stopped existing when the System told him to smile.”
He smokes code, bleeds static, and believes revolution must first be performed before it can be won.
Elias was born in Neue Hamburg, heart of the Großdeutsches Konsortium’s music industry.
A prodigy composer turned anti-corporate lyricist, his band’s final album — “Black Data Halo” — was banned after its hidden track triggered neural implants to broadcast forbidden frequencies.
When the authorities raided his home, he disappeared, leaving behind a bloodied guitar and a smear of code across the floor that simply read:
“DELETE ELIAS. RUN RAFE.”

Rafe Virex is less a man than an infection in the system — a memetic ghost.
His signature mark: a stylized “V//” sigil burned into corrupted data clusters.
His voice is rumored to be carried on dead frequencies — the kind only old analog radios can catch.
Followers call themselves “The Resonant” — those who “still hear the signal.”

#Net #Canon
#Net #Canon
Prime Solutions Model 79 Type .44 Revolver
A heavy, no-nonsense piece of hardware built for the kind of work that leaves bodies cooling on rain-slicked pavement. Issued exclusively to the New Berlin Police Department, this firearm—known in the underworld as the "Dominion Special"—is as much a statement as it is a weapon.
The core of the piece is a heavily modified Steyr Mannlicher .222 SL receiver, fitted with a secondary Charter Arms Bulldog revolver frame chambered in .44 Special. A hybrid design—part automatic, part wheelgun—giving it stopping power meant for more than just flesh-and-blood targets. The weight alone makes it a beast to carry, but when you need to put something down, it’s a comforting weight in the hand.
Twin triggers control the two firing mechanisms—one for the semi-auto upper, one for the revolver cylinder below. The six-shot rotating chamber carries high-grain hollow points, ideal for breaking through synthetic muscle and polymer-reinforced bone plating. The auto-loader up top? That’s for controlled fire, sending out high-velocity slugs when you need precision over brute force.
The frame is all blackened steel and Bakelite, built to withstand the acid rain and the grime of the current Earth Atmosphere. The grip—heavy, textured, and ergonomic—fits snug against the palm, its weight a reminder of its purpose. Along the barrel, a red LED readout blinks softly in the dark.
Silent when holstered, thunderous when drawn—this is the gun you carry when the job isn’t about keeping the peace, but enforcing it.

#Net #Canon
#Net #Canon
The Großdeutsches Konsortium (GDK) is not just a government—it is an economic empire, a technocratic corporate syndicate that has subsumed all of Europe under its relentless efficiency. Borders have been erased, national identities repurposed, and cultures homogenized under the cold, calculating rule of megacorporations, industrial cartels, and cybernetic bureaucracies.
Rather than a traditional government, the GDK is ruled by a Board of Directors, an oligarchic council comprised of the most powerful corporate CEOs, technocrats, and industrial magnates. These figures operate in secrecy, their decisions dictated by predictive AI models and profit-driven algorithms rather than human morality. Parliament exists in name only—policy is dictated by corporate necessity, not democracy.
Below them, departmental Kommissars oversee key sectors:
Das Ministerium für Ordnung (The Ministry of Order) – A paramilitary police force controlling the population through cybernetic enforcers and AI-driven surveillance.
Die Wirtschaftsleitung (The Economic Directorate) – Governs all commerce, labor, and financial systems, ensuring an optimized and compliant workforce.
Die Wissenschaftliche Behörde (The Scientific Authority) – Develops bio-mechanical augmentation, cybernetic AI, and weaponized automation under strict corporate secrecy.
Das Informationsbüro (The Information Bureau) – Controls media, propaganda, and digital surveillance, rewriting history in real time to ensure corporate supremacy.
Life under the GDK is defined by rigid economic class structures, mandatory cybernetic integration, and an obsession with order and productivity. Citizens are classified into strict castes based on their value to the Consortium:
Direktoren (Executives) – The elite ruling class, genetically optimized and cybernetically enhanced to extend their lifespans and intelligence.
Verwaltungskaste (Administrator Caste) – Bureaucrats and middle-management cyber-officials who maintain the GDK’s endless logistical machine.
Fachkräfte (Skilled Workforce) – Engineers, scientists, and technicians who design and maintain the infrastructure of the state.
Arbeiterklasse (Labor Class) – Cybernetically-enhanced workers bound to industrial megafactories, assigned to endless shifts with neural productivity implants.
Nutzlose (The Useless) – The unemployed, criminals, and societal rejects, often repurposed as test subjects, cyber-slaves, or neural processors for AI systems.

Architecture – Brutalist megastructures, industrial skylines dominated by corporate towers with massive propaganda screens, and underground infrastructure layers filled with forgotten slums.
Technology – Clunky, analog-inspired cybernetics, bio-mechanical automation, and a reliance on hardwired networks instead of cloud-based AI.
Military & Law Enforcement – The Ordnungswache (Order Watch), a heavily armed corporate police force clad in reinforced riot armor with glowing red visors, assisted by automated hunter-killer drones and cybernetic hounds.
Despite its iron grip, the GDK faces resistance. Hacktivists, cyber-mercenaries, and defecting scientists operate in the shadows, forming hidden cells across abandoned metro tunnels, forgotten industrial zones, and derelict spaceports. The largest opposition force is rumored to be “Das Schwarze Netz” (The Black Net)—a decentralized underground movement fighting to break the Consortium’s control over human consciousness itself.
The ultimate goal of the Großdeutsches Konsortium is not just economic dominance—it is total optimization of the human condition. Whether through forced cybernetic augmentation, predictive AI control, or neural reprogramming, the GDK seeks to eliminate inefficiency at all costs.
For the Consortium, free will is an obstacle. Compliance is progress. Humanity is an asset to be refined.

#Net #Canon
#Net #Canon
A post-Soviet, neo-industrial superpower, Красная Звезда (Krasnaya Zvezda, The Red Star) is a vast, iron-fisted empire stretching across the frozen wastes of Siberia, the industrial heartlands of the Urals, and the war-ravaged territories of Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Unlike the hyper-capitalist Großdeutsches Konsortium, the Red Star presents itself as a workers’ utopia—but in reality, it is a relentless, authoritarian machine where human lives are just another raw material to be processed.
At the head of Krasnaya Zvezda is the Совет Верховных Комиссаров (Soviet Verkhovnykh Komissarov, The Supreme Commissariat)—a ruling body of technocrats, military leaders, and ideological enforcers. They act under the shadow of a mysterious central AI directive known only as "Заря" (Zarya, "Dawn"), a superintelligent machine guiding the Red Star’s policies toward its ultimate goal: perpetual industrial expansion and war.
Государственная Безопасность (Gosudarstvennaya Bezopasnost, GB) – The brutal secret police, cybernetically-enhanced and enforcing absolute obedience through fear.
Народная Индустриальная Коллегия (Narodnaya Industrial’naya Kollegiya, NIK) – The Industrial People's Collegium, controlling all factories, labor forces, and technological development.
Красный Космос (Krasny Kosmos) – The Red Cosmos, a state-led effort to dominate space with orbital platforms, cybernetic satellite networks, and weaponized space stations.
Великая Освободительная Армия (Velikaya Osvoboditelnaya Armiya, VOA) – The Great Liberation Army, a massive force of conscripts, mechanized troops, and cybernetic shock soldiers that relentlessly push the Red Star’s borders outward.
Life in Krasnaya Zvezda is harsh, cold, and brutally efficient. Every citizen is assigned a role at birth based on their genetic profile, physical ability, and ideological compliance. The state classifies people into rigid castes based on their usefulness:
Инженеры (Inzhenerï, Engineers) – The intellectual elite, responsible for cybernetics, war machines, and AI development. Often treated better, but under strict ideological scrutiny.
Солдаты (Soldaty, Soldiers) – The backbone of the state, most of them enhanced with cheap cybernetics, exoskeletons, or neural implants to increase battlefield efficiency.
Рабочие (Rabochiye, Workers) – The industrial workforce, either assigned to factory complexes, mining operations, or power plants. Many are partially augmented to work faster and longer.
Бесполезные (Bespoleznye, The Useless) – The crippled, the rebellious, and the undesirable—often used as test subjects for cybernetic experiments or sent to labor camps deep in the Siberian tundra.
Unlike the corporate cybernetics of the GDK, where augmentations are sleek and high-end, Krasnaya Zvezda's cybernetics are brutal, industrial, and crude. Limbs are replaced with piston-driven arms, neural interfaces are hardwired directly into the skull, and some citizens are transformed into semi-mechanical drones, their bodies repurposed for endless labor or war.
A core aspect of the Red Star's ideology is "The Flesh is Weak"—humanity must be perfected through machinery. However, many in the lower castes fear they are being stripped of their souls, becoming little more than organic components in the state's vast industrial engine.

Architecture – Colossal Soviet brutalist megastructures, filled with smokestacks belching black smog, with massive propaganda murals of cybernetically-enhanced soldiers and workers.
Technology – Cold War-era machinery fused with clunky cybernetics, nuclear-powered war machines, and hardwired AI control systems. The tech is rugged, industrial, and built to last—even if it dehumanizes its users.
Urban Life – Cities are monolithic industrial zones, where red neon and propaganda screens cast an eerie glow over streets filled with exhaust-choked air, cybernetic enforcers, and ever-present state surveillance.
Rural Zones – Vast, snow-covered wastelands where mining operations, hidden bunkers, and forced labor camps extract resources for the endless war machine.
Krasnaya Zvezda and the GDK are locked in a cold war, a massive geopolitical struggle between corporate-driven hyper-capitalism and authoritarian industrial communism.
The Red Star views the GDK as a decadent, corrupt society ruled by "greedy pigs and machine overlords." It believes Europe must be "liberated" from corporate slavery, even if it means destroying it in the process.
The GDK sees the Red Star as a barbaric, primitive regime—a war-torn relic that refuses to evolve beyond industrial brute force and ideological fanaticism.
The border regions between the two superpowers are endless battlefields, where cybernetic shock troops, mechanized war machines, and AI-controlled drones clash in nightmarish industrial warfare.
The ultimate goal of the Red Star is total industrial and ideological domination. Its rulers believe that humanity’s future lies in the merging of flesh and machine—but not as individuals, rather as a single, unified war engine.
Individuality is weakness.
Freedom is a lie.
The machine must march forward.
